children.translated_text: <s>Nāgārjuna</s>-composed <s>Madhyamakaśāstra</s> (Treatise on the Middle Way) / (Mś)
1. <s>Pratyayaparīkṣā</s> (Examination of Conditions), the first chapter.
Neither cessation nor arising, neither annihilation nor permanence,
neither one meaning nor many meanings, neither coming nor going. // Mś 1.1 //
He who taught <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), the auspicious cessation of <s>prapañca</s> (conceptual proliferation),

children.text: deśayāmāsa saṃbuddhastaṃ vande vadatāṃ varam // Mś_1.2 //
children.translated_text: to that fully awakened <s>Saṃbuddha</s>, the best of teachers, I pay homage. // Mś 1.2 //

children.text: na svato nāpi parato na dvābhyāṃ nāpyahetutaḥ /
children.translated_text: Not from themselves, nor from another, nor from both, nor without a cause,

children.text: utpannā jātu vidyante bhāvāḥ kkacana kecana // Mś_1.3 //
children.translated_text: do any things whatsoever ever arise anywhere. // Mś 1.3 //
There are four <s>pratyayas</s> (conditions): <s>hetu</s> (cause), <s>ālambana</s> (object-support), <s>anantara</s> (immediately preceding),

children.text: tathaivādhipateyaṃ ca pratyayo nāsti pañcamaḥ // Mś_1.4 //
children.translated_text: and likewise <s>adhipati</s> (dominant condition); there is no fifth condition. // Mś 1.4 //

children.text: na hi svabhāvo bhāvānāṃ pratyayādiṣu vidyate /
children.translated_text: For the <s>svabhāva</s> (inherent nature) of things is not found in conditions and so forth;

children.text: avidyamāne svabhāve parabhāvo na vidyate // Mś_1.5 //
children.translated_text: when <s>svabhāva</s> (inherent nature) is not found, <s>parabhāva</s> (other-nature) is not found either. // Mś 1.5 //
Action does not possess conditions, nor is action devoid of conditions;
conditions are not devoid of action, nor do they possess action. // Mś 1.6 //
'It arises dependent on these, therefore these are conditions' —
so long as it has not arisen, why are they not non-conditions? // Mś 1.7 //
A condition is fitting neither for a non-existent thing nor for an existent thing;

children.text: asataḥ pratyayaḥ kasya sataśca pratyayena kim // Mś_1.8 //
children.translated_text: of what non-existent thing would there be a condition? And what use is a condition for what already exists? // Mś 1.8 //

children.text: na sannāsanna sadasan dharmo nirvartate yadā /
children.translated_text: When a <s>dharma</s> that is neither existent, nor non-existent, nor both existent and non-existent is not produced,

children.text: kathaṃ nirvartako heturevaṃ sati hi yujyate // Mś_1.9 //
children.translated_text: how can a producing cause be appropriate in such a case? // Mś 1.9 //
This existent <s>dharma</s> is taught to be without an object-support;

children.text: athānālambane dharme kuta ālambanaṃ punaḥ // Mś_1.10 //
children.translated_text: and if the <s>dharma</s> is without an object-support, where then is the <s>ālambana</s> (object-support condition)? // Mś 1.10 //
When <s>dharmas</s> have not yet arisen, <s>nirodha</s> (cessation) is not tenable;

children.text: nānantaramato yuktaṃ niruddhe pratyayaśca kaḥ // Mś_1.11 //
children.translated_text: therefore the immediately preceding condition is not appropriate, and what is a condition for what has ceased? // Mś 1.11 //

children.text: bhāvānāṃ niḥsvabhāvānāṃ na sattā vidyate yataḥ /
children.translated_text: Since the existence of things devoid of <s>svabhāva</s> (inherent nature) is not found,
the statement 'when this exists, that comes to be' is simply not tenable. // Mś 1.12 //
The result does not exist in conditions, whether taken separately or collectively;

children.text: pratyayebhyaḥ kathaṃ tacca bhavenna pratyayeṣu yat // Mś_1.13 //
children.translated_text: how can that which is not in the conditions come into being from the conditions? // Mś 1.13 //
And if a non-existent result proceeds from those conditions,
why does a result not proceed also from non-conditions? // Mś 1.14 //
The result is made of conditions, but the conditions are not even made of themselves;
how can a result that comes from what is not self-made be made of conditions? // Mś 1.15 //
Therefore the result is neither made of conditions nor made of non-conditions;
since the result is not found, where then are conditions or non-conditions? // Mś 1.16 //
2. <s>Gatāgataparīkṣā</s> (Examination of What Has Gone and What Has Not Gone), the second chapter.

children.text: gataṃ na gamyate tāvadagataṃ naiva gamyate /
children.translated_text: What has been gone to is not being gone to; what has not yet been gone to is likewise not being gone to;
and the presently-being-gone-to, separated from what has been gone to and what has not been gone to, is not being gone to. // Mś 2.1 //

children.text: ceṣṭā yatra gatistatra gamyamāne ca sā yataḥ /
children.translated_text: Where there is movement, there is motion, and since that movement is in the presently-being-gone-to,

children.text: na gate nāgate ceṣṭā gamyamāne gatistataḥ // Mś_2.2 //
children.translated_text: not in what has been gone to nor in what has not been gone to, motion is in the presently-being-gone-to. // Mś 2.2 //
How indeed could motion of the presently-being-gone-to be tenable,
when a double going in the presently-being-gone-to is simply not tenable? // Mś 2.3 //
For whoever holds that there is motion of the presently-being-gone-to,

children.text: ṛte gatergamyamānaṃ gamyamānaṃ hi gamyate // Mś_2.4 //
children.translated_text: it follows that there is a presently-being-gone-to without motion, for the presently-being-gone-to is being gone to. // Mś 2.4 //
If motion belongs to the presently-being-gone-to, a double going follows:

children.text: yena tadgamyamānaṃ ca yaccātra gamanaṃ punaḥ // Mś_2.5 //
children.translated_text: that by which it is presently-being-gone-to, and the going itself that is there again. // Mś 2.5 //
Two goers would follow from the double going that is entailed,

children.text: gantāraṃ hi tiraskṛtya gamanaṃ nopapadyate // Mś_2.6 //
children.translated_text: for without a goer, going is not tenable. // Mś 2.6 //
If, without a goer, going is not tenable,

children.text: gamane 'sati gantātha kuta eva bhaviṣyati // Mś_2.7 //
children.translated_text: then in the absence of going, how could a goer come to be? // Mś 2.7 //

children.text: gantā na gacchati tāvadagantā naiva gacchati /
children.translated_text: A goer does not go, and a non-goer certainly does not go;

children.text: anyo ganturagantuśca kastṛtīyo hi gacchati // Mś_2.8 //
children.translated_text: what third one other than the goer and the non-goer goes? // Mś 2.8 //
How indeed could the proposition 'a goer goes' be tenable,

children.text: gamanena vinā gantā yadā naivopapadyate // Mś_2.9 //
children.translated_text: when without going a goer is simply not tenable? // Mś 2.9 //

children.text: pakṣo gantā gacchatīti yasya tasya prasajyate /
children.translated_text: For whoever holds the thesis that a goer goes,
there follows a goer without going, since he desires going of a goer. // Mś 2.10 //

children.text: gamane dve prasajyete gantā yadyuta gacchati /
children.translated_text: Two goings would follow if a goer goes:

children.text: ganteti cocyate yena gantā san yacca gacchati // Mś_2.11 //
children.translated_text: the going by which he is called a goer, and the going which the goer, being a goer, goes. // Mś 2.11 //
Going is not begun in what has been gone to; going is not begun in what has not been gone to;
going is not begun in the presently-being-gone-to — where then is going begun? // Mś 2.12 //

children.text: na pūrvaṃ gamanārambhādgamyamānaṃ na vā gatam /
children.translated_text: Prior to the beginning of going, there is neither the presently-being-gone-to nor the gone-to
in which going could begin; how could there be going in the not-yet-gone-to? // Mś 2.13 //

children.text: gataṃ kiṃ gamyamānaṃ kimagataṃ kiṃ vikalpyate /
children.translated_text: What is the gone-to? What is the being-gone-to? What is the not-yet-gone-to? — so one may speculate,
when the beginning of going is in no way seen. // Mś 2.14 //

children.text: gantā na tiṣṭhati tāvadagantā naiva tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: A goer does not stop, and a non-goer certainly does not stop;
what third one other than the goer and the non-goer stops? // Mś 2.15 //
How indeed could the proposition 'a goer stops' be tenable,

children.text: gamanena vinā gantā yadā naivopapadyate // Mś_2.16 //
children.translated_text: when without going a goer is simply not tenable? // Mś 2.16 //
One does not come to rest from the presently-being-gone-to, nor from the gone-to, nor from the not-yet-gone-to;

children.text: gamanaṃ saṃpravṛttiśca nivṛttiśca gateḥ samā // Mś_2.17 //
children.translated_text: going, origination, and cessation are the same as motion [in their analysis]. // Mś 2.17 //

children.text: yadeva gamanaṃ gantā sa eveti na yujyate /
children.translated_text: That the going itself is the goer — this is not tenable;

children.text: anya eva punargantā gateriti na yujyate // Mś_2.18 //
children.translated_text: that the goer is something other than the going — this too is not tenable. // Mś 2.18 //

children.text: yadeva gamanaṃ gantā sa eva hi bhavedyadi /
children.translated_text: If the going itself were the goer,

children.text: ekībhāvaḥ prasajyeta kartuḥ karmaṇa eva ca // Mś_2.19 //
children.translated_text: it would follow that agent and action are identical. // Mś 2.19 //
If, on the other hand, the goer is conceived as different from the going,
there would be going without a goer and a goer without going. // Mś 2.20 //
Neither through identity nor through difference is establishment possible for these two;

children.text: na vidyate, tayoḥ siddhiḥ kathaṃ nu khalu vidyate // Mś_2.21 //
children.translated_text: when they are not established [by either], how indeed could they be established? // Mś 2.21 //

children.text: gatyā yayocyate gantā gatiṃ tāṃ sa na gacchati /
children.translated_text: The goer does not go by that going through which he is designated a goer,
for he does not exist prior to that going — who goes where? // Mś 2.22 //

children.text: gatyā yayocyate gantā tato 'nyāṃ sa na gacchati /
children.translated_text: The goer does not go by a going other than that through which he is designated a goer,

children.text: gatī dve nopapadyete yasmādeke pragacchati // Mś_2.23 //
children.translated_text: for two goings are not tenable in one who goes. // Mś 2.23 //

children.text: sadbhūto gamanaṃ gantā triprakāraṃ na gacchati /
children.translated_text: A really existent goer does not perform a threefold going;

children.text: nāsadbhūto 'pi gamanaṃ triprakāraṃ sa gacchati // Mś_2.24 //
children.translated_text: nor does a non-existent goer perform a threefold going. // Mś 2.24 //
A goer that is both existent and non-existent does not perform a threefold going;

children.text: tasmādgatiśca gantā ca gantavyaṃ ca na vidyate // Mś_2.25 //
children.translated_text: therefore, motion, the goer, and the path to be traversed do not exist [as inherently real]. // Mś 2.25 //
3. <s>Cakṣurādīndriyaparīkṣā</s> (Examination of the Sense Organs such as the Eye), the third chapter.

children.text: darśanaṃ śravaṇaṃ ghrāṇaṃ rasanaṃ sparśanaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting, touching, and the mind —
these are the six <s>indriyas</s> (sense faculties); the visible and so forth are their domains. // Mś 3.1 //

children.text: svamātmānaṃ darśanaṃ hi tattameva na paśyati /
children.translated_text: Seeing does not see its own self;

children.text: na paśyati yadātmānaṃ kathaṃ drakṣyati tatparān // Mś_3.2 //
children.translated_text: if it does not see itself, how can it see others? // Mś 3.2 //
The analogy of fire is not sufficient to establish seeing;
that [analogy] together with seeing has been refuted by the [analysis of the] presently-being-gone-to, the gone-to, and the not-yet-gone-to. // Mś 3.3 //
When seeing is not seeing anything at all,
how is it tenable to say 'seeing sees'? // Mś 3.4 //
Seeing itself does not see, and non-seeing certainly does not see;
the seer too should be understood as explained by [the analysis of] seeing itself. // Mś 3.5 //
Without seeing, no seer exists; and without the seer, no seeing exists;

children.text: draṣṭavyaṃ darśanaṃ caiva draṣṭaryasati te kutaḥ // Mś_3.6 //
children.translated_text: when the seer does not exist, where then are the visible object and seeing? // Mś 3.6 //
Just as the birth of a son is said to depend on the mother and father,
so the arising of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is said to depend on the eye and visible form. // Mś 3.7 //
Due to the non-existence of the visible object and seeing, the fourfold group beginning with <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness)

children.text: nāstīti upādānādīni bhaviṣyanti punaḥ katham // Mś_3.8 //
children.translated_text: does not exist — how then will <s>upādāna</s> (grasping) and the rest come to be? // Mś 3.8 //

children.text: vyākhyātaṃ śravaṇaṃ ghrāṇaṃ rasanaṃ sparśanaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing, smelling, tasting, touching, and the mind are explained
by the analysis of seeing itself; one should understand the hearer, the audible, and so forth likewise. // Mś 3.9 //
4. <s>Skandhaparīkṣā</s> (Examination of the Aggregates), the fourth chapter.
<s>Rūpa</s> (form) is not apprehended apart from the cause of form;

children.text: rūpeṇāpi na nirmuktaṃ dṛśyate rūpakāraṇam // Mś_4.1 //
children.translated_text: nor is the cause of form seen apart from <s>rūpa</s> (form). // Mś 4.1 //
If <s>rūpa</s> (form) were apart from its cause, form would follow

children.text: āhetukaṃ, na cāstyarthaḥ kaścidāhetukaḥ kvacit // Mś_4.2 //
children.translated_text: as causeless; but there is no thing anywhere that is without a cause. // Mś 4.2 //
If the cause of form were apart from <s>rūpa</s> (form),

children.text: akāryakaṃ kāraṇaṃ syāt nāstyakāryaṃ ca kāraṇam // Mś_4.3 //
children.translated_text: the cause would be without an effect; but there is no cause without an effect. // Mś 4.3 //
When <s>rūpa</s> (form) exists, a cause of form is not tenable;
when <s>rūpa</s> (form) does not exist, a cause of form is not tenable either. // Mś 4.4 //
<s>Rūpa</s> (form) without a cause is simply not tenable at all;

children.text: tasmāt rūpagatān kāṃścinna vikalpān vikalpayet // Mś_4.5 //
children.translated_text: therefore one should not entertain any conceptions whatsoever regarding form. // Mś 4.5 //
It is not tenable that an effect is similar to its cause;
it is not tenable that an effect is dissimilar to its cause. // Mś 4.6 //
Of <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>citta</s> (mind), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), and <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations),

children.text: sarveṣāmeva bhāvānāṃ rūpeṇaiva samaḥ kramaḥ // Mś_4.7 //
children.translated_text: and of all things whatsoever, the procedure is the same as with <s>rūpa</s> (form). // Mś 4.7 //

children.text: vigrahe yaḥ parīhāraṃ kṛte śūnyatayā vadet /
children.translated_text: Whoever would answer an objection by means of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness),

children.text: sarvaṃ tasyāparihṛtaṃ samaṃ sādhyena jāyate // Mś_4.8 //
children.translated_text: for him everything remains unanswered, being equivalent to what is to be proved. // Mś 4.8 //

children.text: vyākhyāne ya upālambhaṃ kṛte śūnyatayā vadet /
children.translated_text: Whoever would criticize an explanation made by means of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness),

children.text: sarvaṃ tasyānupālabdhaṃ samaṃ sādhyena jāyate // Mś_4.9 //
children.translated_text: for him everything remains uncriticized, being equivalent to what is to be proved. // Mś 4.9 //
5. <s>Dhātuparīkṣā</s> (Examination of the Elements), the fifth chapter.
Space does not exist at all prior to the defining characteristic of space;

children.text: alakṣaṇaṃ prasajyeta syātpūrvaṃ yadi lakṣaṇāt // Mś_5.1 //
children.translated_text: if it existed prior to its characteristic, it would follow that it is without a defining characteristic. // Mś 5.1 //

children.text: alakṣaṇo na kaścicca bhāvaḥ saṃvidyate kkacit /
children.translated_text: No entity whatsoever without a defining characteristic is found anywhere;

children.text: asatyalakṣaṇe bhāve kramatāṃ kuha lakṣaṇam // Mś_5.2 //
children.translated_text: when no entity without a characteristic exists, to what does the characteristic apply? // Mś 5.2 //
The characteristic does not operate in what is without a characteristic, nor in what has a characteristic;
nor does it operate in something other than what has and what lacks a characteristic. // Mś 5.3 //
When the characteristic does not operate, the characterized is not tenable;
and when the characterized is not tenable, the characteristic too is impossible. // Mś 5.4 //

children.text: tasmānna vidyate lakṣyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ naiva vidyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore the characterized does not exist, and the characteristic does not exist;
nor does any entity apart from the characterized and the characteristic exist. // Mś 5.5 //
When an entity does not exist, of what will there be non-existence?
And who knows entity and non-entity, being different from both entity and non-entity? // Mś 5.6 //

children.text: tasmānna bhāvo nābhāvo na lakṣyaṃ nāpi lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, neither entity, nor non-entity, nor the characterized, nor the characteristic;

children.text: ākāśam ākāśasamā dhātavaḥ pañca ye pare // Mś_5.7 //
children.translated_text: space and the five remaining <s>dhātus</s> (elements) are the same as space [in this analysis]. // Mś 5.7 //

children.text: astitvaṃ ye tu paśyanti nāstitvaṃ cālpabuddhayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those of little understanding who perceive the existence

children.text: bhāvānāṃ te na paśyanti draṣṭavyopaśamaṃ śivam // Mś_5.8 //
children.translated_text: and non-existence of things do not see the auspicious cessation of the visible. // Mś 5.8 //
6. <s>Rāgaraktaparīkṣā</s> (Examination of Passion and the Impassioned), the sixth chapter.
If the impassioned one existed prior to passion, independent of passion,

children.text: taṃ pratītya bhavedrāgo rakte rāgo bhavetsati // Mś_6.1 //
children.translated_text: then passion would arise dependent on him — passion would exist when an impassioned one exists. // Mś 6.1 //

children.text: rakte 'sati punā rāgaḥ kuta eva bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: But when there is no impassioned one, how could passion come to be?

children.text: sati vāsati vā rāge rakte 'pyeṣa samaḥ kramaḥ // Mś_6.2 //
children.translated_text: Whether passion exists or not, the same procedure applies to the impassioned one as well. // Mś 6.2 //
Moreover, the simultaneous arising of passion and the impassioned is not tenable,

children.text: bhavetāṃ rāgaraktau hi nirapekṣau parasparam // Mś_6.3 //
children.translated_text: for then passion and the impassioned would be mutually independent. // Mś 6.3 //

children.text: naikatve sahabhāvo 'sti na tenaiva hi tatsaha /
children.translated_text: In identity there is no co-existence, for a thing is not co-existent with itself;

children.text: pṛthaktve sahabhāvo 'tha kuta eva bhaviṣyati // Mś_6.4 //
children.translated_text: but in difference, how could co-existence ever come to be? // Mś 6.4 //
If co-existence were possible in identity, it would exist even without a companion;
if co-existence were possible in difference, it would exist even without a companion. // Mś 6.5 //
If co-existence were possible in difference, what is it about passion and the impassioned
that their separate existence is established, such that there is co-existence of the two? // Mś 6.6 //
If indeed the separate existence of passion and the impassioned were established,

children.text: sahabhāvaṃ kimarthaṃ tu parikalpayase tayoḥ // Mś_6.7 //
children.translated_text: for what purpose do you then imagine co-existence of the two? // Mś 6.7 //
Because separateness is not established, you seek co-existence;
and for the purpose of establishing co-existence, you desire separateness again. // Mś 6.8 //
Since separateness is not established, co-existence is not established;
in what kind of separateness do you wish co-existence to be present? // Mś 6.9 //

children.text: evaṃ raktena rāgasya siddhirna saha nāsaha /
children.translated_text: Thus passion is not established either together with or apart from the impassioned one;
like passion, no <s>dharmas</s> (things) whatsoever are established either together with or apart from [their counterparts]. // Mś 6.10 //
7. <s>Saṃskṛtaparīkṣā</s> (Examination of the Conditioned), the seventh chapter.
If <s>utpāda</s> (arising) is conditioned, then the three characteristics are appropriate for it;
but if <s>utpāda</s> (arising) is unconditioned, how can it be a characteristic of the conditioned? // Mś 7.1 //
The three — arising and the rest — taken separately, are not capable of performing the function of characterizing
the conditioned; how could they be combined all together in one place at one time? // Mś 7.2 //
If <s>utpāda</s> (arising), <s>sthiti</s> (duration), and <s>bhaṅga</s> (destruction) each have another conditioned characteristic,

children.text: asti cedanavasthaivaṃ nāsti cette na saṃskṛtāḥ // Mś_7.3 //
children.translated_text: there is an infinite regress; if they do not, then they are not conditioned. // Mś 7.3 //
The arising of arising is only the arising of the primary arising;
and the primary arising in turn produces the arising of arising. // Mś 7.4 //
If, according to you, the arising of arising is the arising of the primary arising,

children.text: maulenājanitastaṃ te sa kathaṃ janayiṣyati // Mś_7.5 //
children.translated_text: how will that [arising of arising], not yet produced by the primary arising, produce it? // Mś 7.5 //

children.text: sa te maulena janito maulaṃ janayate yadi /
children.translated_text: If, according to you, that which is produced by the primary arising produces the primary arising,
how does the primary arising, not yet produced by it, produce it? // Mś 7.6 //
This one, while still arising, would indeed produce that one,
if this one, while still unborn, were able to produce that one. // Mś 7.7 //
Just as a lamp illuminates both itself and others,
so <s>utpāda</s> (arising) would produce both itself and others. // Mś 7.8 //
There is no darkness in a lamp, nor where it is established.

children.text: kiṃ prakāśayati dīpaḥ prakāśo hi tamovadhaḥ // Mś_7.9 //
children.translated_text: What does the lamp illuminate? For illumination is the destruction of darkness. // <s>Mś</s> 7.9 //
How is darkness destroyed by a lamp that is [still] arising?

children.text: notpadyamāno hi tamaḥ pradīpaḥ prāpnute yadā // Mś_7.10 //
children.translated_text: For the lamp, while arising, does not reach the darkness. // <s>Mś</s> 7.10 //

children.text: aprāpyaiva pradīpena yadi vā nihataṃ tamaḥ /
children.translated_text: If, alternatively, darkness is destroyed by the lamp without reaching it,

children.text: ihasthaḥ sarvalokasthaṃ sa tamo nihaniṣyati // Mś_7.11 //
children.translated_text: [then a lamp] situated here would destroy the darkness present in all the worlds. // <s>Mś</s> 7.11 //
If a lamp illuminates both itself and others,
darkness too will without doubt conceal both itself and others. // <s>Mś</s> 7.12 //
This arising, being unarisen, how could it produce itself?

children.text: athotpanno janayate jāte kiṃ janyate punaḥ // Mś_7.13 //
children.translated_text: And if [it is] already arisen, what is produced again when it has [already] been born? // <s>Mś</s> 7.13 //
In no way does that which is arising, that which has arisen, or that which has not arisen
undergo arising — this has been explained [in the same manner] as the gone-to, the going-to, and the not-yet-gone-to. // <s>Mś</s> 7.14 //
When that which is arising does not proceed without arising,
how can that which is arising be said to arise dependently? // <s>Mś</s> 7.15 //
Whatever arises dependently, that is peaceful (<s>śānta</s>) by its own nature.
Therefore, that which is arising is peaceful, and arising itself is [also peaceful]. // <s>Mś</s> 7.16 //
If some unarisen entity were to be found somewhere,

children.text: utpadyeta sa kiṃ tasmin bhāva utpadyate 'sati // Mś_7.17 //
children.translated_text: it might arise. But when that entity does not exist, what arises? // <s>Mś</s> 7.17 //
If arising produces that which is [in the process of] arising,
which arising, in turn, would produce that arising? // <s>Mś</s> 7.18 //
If another arising produces it, there is an infinite regress.
But if [something] arises without [prior] arising, then everything would arise in the same way. // <s>Mś</s> 7.19 //
The arising of an existent [thing] is not tenable, nor [is the arising] of a non-existent [thing].
Nor of [a thing that is] both existent and non-existent — this has been demonstrated previously. // <s>Mś</s> 7.20 //
The arising of an entity that is [in the process of] ceasing is not tenable.
And an entity that is not ceasing is [also] not tenable. // <s>Mś</s> 7.21 //
An established entity does not abide; a non-established entity does not abide;

children.text: na tiṣṭhati tiṣṭhamānaḥ ko 'nutpannaśca tiṣṭhati // Mś_7.22 //
children.translated_text: that which is [in the process of] abiding does not abide — and what unarisen [thing] abides? // <s>Mś</s> 7.22 //
The abiding of an entity that is [in the process of] ceasing is not tenable.
And an entity that is not ceasing is [also] not tenable. // <s>Mś</s> 7.23 //
Since all entities are always subject to the law of decay and death,

children.text: tiṣṭhanti katame bhāvā ye jarāmaraṇaṃ vinā // Mś_7.24 //
children.translated_text: which entities are there that abide without decay and death? // <s>Mś</s> 7.24 //

children.text: sthityānyayā sthiteḥ sthānaṃ tayaiva ca na yujyate /
children.translated_text: Abiding through another [state] of abiding, or through the same [state] — neither is tenable,

children.text: utpādasya yathotpādo nātmanā na parātmanā // Mś_7.25 //
children.translated_text: just as the arising of arising [is not established] either by itself or by another. // <s>Mś</s> 7.25 //
That which has not ceased does not cease; that which has ceased does not cease;
nor does that which is [in the process of] ceasing — and how could that which is unborn cease? // <s>Mś</s> 7.26 //
The cessation of an entity that is established is not tenable,
nor is the cessation of an entity that is not established tenable. // <s>Mś</s> 7.27 //
A state is not destroyed by that very same state,
nor is a state destroyed by a different state. // <s>Mś</s> 7.28 //
When the arising of all <s>dharma</s>s (phenomena) is not tenable in this way,
then the cessation of all <s>dharma</s>s is likewise not tenable. // <s>Mś</s> 7.29 //
The cessation of an existent entity is not tenable,

children.text: ekatve na hi bhāvaśca nābhāvaścopapadyate // Mś_7.30 //
children.translated_text: for being and non-being cannot belong to one and the same thing. // <s>Mś</s> 7.30 //
The cessation of a non-existent entity is also not tenable,

children.text: na dvitīyasya śirasacchedanaṃ vidyate yathā // Mś_7.31 //
children.translated_text: just as the cutting off of a second head does not occur. // <s>Mś</s> 7.31 //

children.text: na svātmanā nirodho 'sti nirodho na parātmanā /
children.translated_text: There is no cessation by itself, nor cessation by another,

children.text: utpādasya yathotpādo nātmanā na parātmanā // Mś_7.32 //
children.translated_text: just as arising does not [occur] by itself nor by another. // <s>Mś</s> 7.32 //
Since arising, abiding, and destruction are not established, the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) does not exist.
And when the conditioned is not established, how will the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>) be established? // <s>Mś</s> 7.33 //

children.text: yathā māyā yathā svapno gandharvanagaraṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: Like an illusion, like a dream, like a city of <s>gandharva</s>s —

children.text: tathotpādastathā sthānaṃ tathā bhaṅga udāhṛtam // Mś_7.34 //
children.translated_text: so arising has been declared, so abiding, so destruction. // <s>Mś</s> 7.34 //
8. Examination of Agent and Action (<s>Karmakārakaparīkṣā</s>), the eighth chapter.

children.text: sadbhūtaḥ kārakaḥ karma sadbhūtaṃ na karotyayam /
children.translated_text: An agent that truly exists does not perform an action that truly exists.
Nor does an agent that does not truly exist undertake an action that does not truly exist. // <s>Mś</s> 8.1 //

children.text: sadbhūtasya kriyā nāsti karma ca syādakartṛkam /
children.translated_text: A truly existent [agent] has no [need for] action, and the action would be without an agent.

children.text: sadbhūtasya kriyā nāsti kartā ca syādakarmakaḥ // Mś_8.2 //
children.translated_text: A truly existent [agent] has no [need for] action, and the agent would be without action. // <s>Mś</s> 8.2 //
If a non-existent agent performs a non-existent action,

children.text: ahetukaṃ bhavetkarma kartā cāhetuko bhavet // Mś_8.3 //
children.translated_text: the action would be without a cause, and the agent would be without a cause. // <s>Mś</s> 8.3 //

children.text: hetāvasati kāryaṃ ca kāraṇaṃ ca na vidyate /
children.translated_text: When a cause does not exist, neither the effect nor the cause is found.

children.text: tadabhāve kriyā kartā karaṇaṃ ca na vidyate // Mś_8.4 //
children.translated_text: In the absence of those, action, agent, and instrument are not found. // <s>Mś</s> 8.4 //
<s>Dharma</s> (virtue) and <s>adharma</s> (vice) are not found when action and the rest are impossible.

children.text: dharme cāsatyadharme ca phalaṃ tajjaṃ na vidyate // Mś_8.5 //
children.translated_text: When <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> do not exist, the fruit born from them is not found. // <s>Mś</s> 8.5 //
When there is no fruit, no path leading to liberation or to heaven

children.text: mārgaḥ sarvakriyāṇāṃ ca nairarthakyaṃ prasajyate // Mś_8.6 //
children.translated_text: is tenable, and the purposelessness of all actions follows. // <s>Mś</s> 8.6 //
An agent that is both existent and non-existent does not perform that [action] which is both existent and non-existent.
For existence and non-existence are mutually contradictory — how can they be in one [thing]? // <s>Mś</s> 8.7 //

children.text: satā ca kriyate nāsannāsatā kriyate ca sat /
children.translated_text: A non-existent [thing] is not made by an existent [agent], nor is an existent [thing] made by a non-existent [agent].

children.text: kartrā sarve prasajyante doṣāstatra ta eva hi // Mś_8.8 //
children.translated_text: With respect to the agent, all the [previously stated] defects follow in these [cases] too. // <s>Mś</s> 8.8 //
An existent agent does not perform an action that is non-existent, existent,

children.text: karoti kārakaḥ karma pūrvoktaireva hetubhiḥ // Mś_8.9 //
children.translated_text: or both existent and non-existent — for the reasons previously stated. // <s>Mś</s> 8.9 //
A non-existent agent too does not perform an action that is existent,

children.text: karoti kārakaḥ karma purvoktaireva hetubhiḥ // Mś_8.10 //
children.translated_text: both existent and non-existent, [or non-existent] — for the reasons previously stated. // <s>Mś</s> 8.10 //
An agent that is both existent and non-existent does not perform an action that is neither existent nor non-existent.
One should understand this for the reasons previously stated. // <s>Mś</s> 8.11 //

children.text: pratītya kārakaḥ karma taṃ pratītya ca kārakam /
children.translated_text: The agent proceeds to action dependently, and the action
depends on the agent. We see no other cause of their establishment. // <s>Mś</s> 8.12 //
In this way one should understand appropriation (<s>upādāna</s>) through the relinquishment of [the notion of independent] action.

children.text: kartuśca karmakartṛbhyāṃ śeṣān bhāvān vibhāvayet // Mś_8.13 //
children.translated_text: Through agent and action, one should discern the remaining entities. // <s>Mś</s> 8.13 //
9. Examination of the Prior Existent (<s>Pūrvaparīkṣā</s>), the ninth chapter.
Seeing, hearing, and the like, as well as feeling and the rest —

children.text: bhavanti yasya prāgebhyaḥ so 'stītyeke vadantyuta // Mś_9.1 //
children.translated_text: some say that the one to whom these belong exists prior to them. // <s>Mś</s> 9.1 //
For how could seeing and the rest belong to something non-existent?

children.text: bhāvasya tasmātprāgebhyaḥ so 'sti bhāvo vyavasthitaḥ // Mś_9.2 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, an entity exists, established prior to them. // <s>Mś</s> 9.2 //
But the entity that is established prior to seeing, hearing, and the like,

children.text: yaḥ prāgvyavasthito bhāvaḥ kena prajñapyate 'tha saḥ // Mś_9.3 //
children.translated_text: and to feeling and the rest — by what is it made known? // <s>Mś</s> 9.3 //
And if it is established even without seeing and the rest,

children.text: amūnyapi bhaviṣyanti vinā tena na saṃśayaḥ // Mś_9.4 //
children.translated_text: these [faculties] too will undoubtedly exist without it. // <s>Mś</s> 9.4 //
Someone is manifested by something; something is manifested by someone.

children.text: kutaḥ kiṃcidvinā kaścit kiṃcitkaṃcidvinā kutaḥ // Mś_9.5 //
children.translated_text: How can someone exist without something, and something without someone? // <s>Mś</s> 9.5 //
No one exists prior to all of seeing, hearing, and the rest.
Rather, through one or another of seeing, etc., one or another [subject] is manifested. // <s>Mś</s> 9.6 //

children.text: sarvebhyo darśanādibhyo yadi pūrvo na vidyate /
children.translated_text: If no one exists prior to all of seeing, hearing, and the rest,

children.text: ekaikasmātkathaṃ pūrvo darśanādeḥ sa vidyate // Mś_9.7 //
children.translated_text: how could one exist prior to each individual one of seeing, etc.? // <s>Mś</s> 9.7 //

children.text: draṣṭā sa eva sa śrotā sa eva yadi vedakaḥ /
children.translated_text: If the seer is the same as the hearer and the same as the feeler,
[then the subject] would exist prior to each [faculty] — and this is not tenable. // <s>Mś</s> 9.8 //
If the seer is different, the hearer different, and the feeler yet another,

children.text: sati syād draṣṭari śrotā bahutvaṃ cātmanāṃ bhavet // Mś_9.9 //
children.translated_text: when there is a seer there would be a hearer [as well], and there would be a multiplicity of selves. // <s>Mś</s> 9.9 //
In the elements from which seeing, hearing, and the like

children.text: bhavanti yebhyasteṣveṣa bhūteṣvapi na vidyate // Mś_9.10 //
children.translated_text: and feeling and the rest arise — [the subject] is not found even in those. // <s>Mś</s> 9.10 //
If seeing, hearing, and the like, as well as feeling and the rest,

children.text: na vidyate cedyasya sa na vidyanta imānyapi // Mś_9.11 //
children.translated_text: do not exist, then that [subject] to whom they [belong] also does not exist, nor do these [faculties]. // <s>Mś</s> 9.11 //

children.text: prāk ca yo darśanādibhyaḥ sāṃprataṃ cordhvameva ca /
children.translated_text: That [subject] who does not exist prior to seeing and the rest, nor at present, nor afterward —

children.text: na vidyate 'sti nāstīti nivṛttāstatra kalpanāḥ // Mś_9.12 //
children.translated_text: with respect to that, conceptualizations of 'exists' and 'does not exist' have ceased. // <s>Mś</s> 9.12 //
10. Examination of Fire and Fuel (<s>Agnīndhanaparīkṣā</s>), the tenth chapter.
If fuel were the same as fire, there would be identity of agent and object.
If fire were different from fuel, fire would exist even apart from fuel. // <s>Mś</s> 10.1 //
It would be eternally burning, not caused by kindling.
Re-ignition would be pointless, and in that case, it would be without action. // <s>Mś</s> 10.2 //
Being independent of another, it would not be caused by kindling.
Re-ignition would be pointless; it would follow that it is eternally burning. // <s>Mś</s> 10.3 //
If [you say:] 'In this case, what is being kindled becomes fuel' —
by what is the fuel kindled, since at that point it is merely this [inert matter]? // <s>Mś</s> 10.4 //

children.text: anyo na prāpsyate 'prāpto na dhakṣyatyadahan punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Being different [from fuel, fire] will not reach [it]; not reaching, it will not burn;

children.text: na nirvāsyatyanirvāṇaḥ sthāsyate vā svaliṅgavān // Mś_10.5 //
children.translated_text: not burning, it will not be extinguished; not being extinguished, it will remain with its own mark. // <s>Mś</s> 10.5 //
If fire, being truly different from fuel, were to reach fuel,

children.text: strī saṃprāpnoti puruṣaṃ puruṣaśca striyaṃ yathā // Mś_10.6 //
children.translated_text: it would be like a woman reaching a man and a man reaching a woman. // <s>Mś</s> 10.6 //
Fire, being truly different from fuel, might indeed reach fuel,
if fire and fuel were to exist while mutually excluded. // <s>Mś</s> 10.7 //
If fire depends on fuel, and fuel depends on fire,
which of the two is established first, on which fire [or] fuel depends? // <s>Mś</s> 10.8 //
If fire depends on fuel, then there is the proof of an already established fire.

children.text: evaṃ satīndhanaṃ cāpi bhaviṣyati niragnikam // Mś_10.9 //
children.translated_text: And in that case, fuel too will exist without fire. // <s>Mś</s> 10.9 //
If a thing is established in dependence on something, and that very thing

children.text: yadi yo 'pekṣitavyaḥ sa sidhyatāṃ kamapekṣya kaḥ // Mś_10.10 //
children.translated_text: is established in dependence on it — if the one that is to be depended upon is [itself] to be established, what depends on what? // <s>Mś</s> 10.10 //
If a thing is established in dependence [on another], how can it, being unestablished, depend [on anything]?
And if it depends while being [already] established, its dependence is not tenable. // <s>Mś</s> 10.11 //
Fire does not exist in dependence on fuel, and fire does not exist independent of fuel.
Fuel does not exist in dependence on fire, and fuel does not exist independent of fire. // <s>Mś</s> 10.12 //
Fire does not come from elsewhere; fire is not found in fuel.
The remainder regarding fuel has been stated [in the same way] as the gone-to, the going-to, and the not-yet-gone-to. // <s>Mś</s> 10.13 //
Fuel is not fire, nor is fire [found] elsewhere than in fuel.
Fire does not possess fuel, nor is fuel in fire, nor fire in them. // <s>Mś</s> 10.14 //
Through [the analysis of] fire and fuel, the entire procedure regarding the self and appropriation (<s>upādāna</s>)
has been explained, together with [examples like] pot, cloth, and the like, without remainder. // <s>Mś</s> 10.15 //

children.text: ātmanaśca satattvaṃ ye bhāvānāṃ ca pṛthakpṛthak /
children.translated_text: Those who declare the self-nature of the self
and of entities, each separately — I do not consider them to be skilled in the meaning of the teaching. // <s>Mś</s> 10.16 //
11. Examination of the Prior and Posterior Limits (<s>Pūrvāparakoṭiparīkṣā</s>), the eleventh chapter.
'A prior limit [of existence] is not known' — thus spoke the Great Sage (<s>Mahāmuni</s>).
<s>Saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence) is without beginning or end; it has no first and no last. // <s>Mś</s> 11.1 //

children.text: naivāgraṃ nāvaraṃ yasya tasya madhyaṃ kuto bhavet /
children.translated_text: For that which has neither a beginning nor an end, how could there be a middle?
Therefore, the sequences of prior, posterior, and simultaneous are not tenable here. // <s>Mś</s> 11.2 //
If birth were first and decay-and-death afterward,
birth would be without decay-and-death, and one would be born immortal. // <s>Mś</s> 11.3 //
If birth were afterward and decay-and-death came first,
how could there be causeless decay-and-death of one who is unborn? // <s>Mś</s> 11.4 //
Birth simultaneous with decay-and-death is also not tenable,
for one would die while being born, and both would be without a cause. // <s>Mś</s> 11.5 //
When the sequences of prior, posterior, and simultaneous are not possible,

children.text: prapañcayanti tāṃ jātiṃ tajjarāmaraṇaṃ ca kim // Mś_11.6 //
children.translated_text: why do [people] elaborate upon that birth and that decay-and-death? // <s>Mś</s> 11.6 //

children.text: kāryaṃ ca kāraṇaṃ caiva lakṣyaṃ lakṣaṇameva ca /
children.translated_text: Effect and cause, the characterized and the characteristic,

children.text: vedanā vedakaścaiva santyarthā ye ca kecana // Mś_11.7 //
children.translated_text: feeling and the feeler — and whatever entities there are — // <s>Mś</s> 11.7 //

children.text: pūrvā na vidyate koṭiḥ saṃsārasya na kevalam /
children.translated_text: not only is a prior limit of <s>saṃsāra</s> not found,

children.text: sarveṣāmapi bhāvānāṃ pūrvā koṭirna vidyate // Mś_11.8 //
children.translated_text: but a prior limit of all entities whatsoever is not found. // <s>Mś</s> 11.8 //
12. Examination of Suffering (<s>Duḥkhaparīkṣā</s>), the twelfth chapter.
Some hold that suffering is self-made, made by another, made by both,

children.text: duḥkhamityeka icchanti tacca kāryaṃ na yujyate // Mś_12.1 //
children.translated_text: or without a cause — but [suffering] as an effect is not tenable [in any of these ways]. // <s>Mś</s> 12.1 //

children.text: svayaṃ kṛtaṃ yadi bhavetpratītya na tato bhavet /
children.translated_text: If [suffering] were self-made, it would not arise dependently.

children.text: skandhānimānamī skandhāḥ saṃbhavanti pratītya hi // Mś_12.2 //
children.translated_text: For these aggregates (<s>skandha</s>s) arise dependent upon those aggregates. // <s>Mś</s> 12.2 //

children.text: yadyamībhya ime 'nye syurebhyo vāmī pare yadi /
children.translated_text: If these [aggregates at one time] were different from those [at another], or if those were other than these,
suffering would be made by another — these [present aggregates] would be made by those [past] others. // <s>Mś</s> 12.3 //
If suffering is made by one's own person (<s>pudgala</s>), then that person, apart from suffering —

children.text: svapudgalaḥ sa katamo yena duḥkhaṃ svayaṃ kṛtam // Mś_12.4 //
children.translated_text: who is that person by whom suffering is self-made? // <s>Mś</s> 12.4 //
If suffering is produced by another person, to whom is it given?

children.text: pareṇa kṛtvā tadduḥkhaṃ sa duḥkhena vinā kutaḥ // Mś_12.5 //
children.translated_text: How could the one to whom that suffering is given — made by another — be without suffering? // <s>Mś</s> 12.5 //
If suffering is produced by another person, who is that other person

children.text: vinā duḥkhena yaḥ kṛtvā parasmai prahiṇoti tat // Mś_12.6 //
children.translated_text: who, being without suffering, makes [it] and sends it to another? // <s>Mś</s> 12.6 //
Since self-made [suffering] is not established, how can suffering be made by another?

children.text: paro hi duḥkhaṃ yatkuryāttattasya syātsvayaṃ kṛtam // Mś_12.7 //
children.translated_text: For the suffering that another would make, that would be self-made for him. // <s>Mś</s> 12.7 //

children.text: na tāvatsvakṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ na hi tenaiva tatkṛtam /
children.translated_text: Suffering is not self-made, for it is not made by that very same [entity].
If another is not made by oneself, how can suffering be made by another? // <s>Mś</s> 12.8 //
Suffering might be made by both if it could be made by each individually.
Suffering not made by another, not self-made — how could it be causeless? // <s>Mś</s> 12.9 //

children.text: na kevalaṃ hi duḥkhasya cāturvidhyaṃ na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Not only does the fourfold [analysis] of suffering not hold —

children.text: bāhyānāmapi bhāvānāṃ cāturvidhyaṃ na vidyate // Mś_12.10 //
children.translated_text: The fourfold [production] of external entities also does not exist. || <s>Mś</s> 12.10 ||
13. Examination of <s>Saṃskāras</s> (Conditioned Things) — the thirteenth chapter.
'That is false, of a deceptive nature' — thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>;

children.text: sarve ca moṣadharmāṇaḥ saṃskārāstena te mṛṣā // Mś_13.1 //
children.translated_text: and all conditioned things (<s>saṃskāras</s>) are of a deceptive nature — therefore they are false. || <s>Mś</s> 13.1 ||

children.text: tanmṛṣā moṣadharma yadyadi kiṃ tatra muṣyate /
children.translated_text: If 'that is false, of a deceptive nature' — then what is deceived therein?
This was said by the <s>Bhagavān</s> as an illumination of emptiness. || <s>Mś</s> 13.2 ||
The absence of intrinsic nature in entities is seen from their becoming otherwise;

children.text: asvabhāvo bhāvo nāsti bhāvānāṃ śūnyatā yataḥ // Mś_13.3 //
children.translated_text: an entity without intrinsic nature does not exist — since that is the emptiness of entities. || <s>Mś</s> 13.3 ||
For what would there be becoming-otherwise, if intrinsic nature does not exist?

children.text: kasya syādanyathābhāvaḥ svabhāvo yadi vidyate // Mś_13.4 //
children.translated_text: For what would there be becoming-otherwise, if intrinsic nature does exist? || <s>Mś</s> 13.4 ||
Becoming-otherwise of that very thing is not [coherent], nor is [becoming-otherwise] of another thing coherent;

children.text: yuvā na jīryate yasmādyasmājjīrṇo na jīryate // Mś_13.5 //
children.translated_text: since a youth does not grow old, and since an old man does not grow old. || <s>Mś</s> 13.5 ||
If there were becoming-otherwise of that very thing, then milk itself would be yogurt;
apart from milk, of what else would there be the state of being yogurt? || <s>Mś</s> 13.6 ||
If something were non-empty, then something might be 'empty';

children.text: na kiṃcidastyaśūnyaṃ ca kutaḥ śūnyaṃ bhaviṣyati // Mś_13.7 //
children.translated_text: since nothing is non-empty — whence will there be 'empty'? || <s>Mś</s> 13.7 ||
Emptiness was proclaimed by the Victorious Ones as the escape from all views;

children.text: yeṣāṃ tu śūnyatā dṛṣṭistānasādhyān babhāṣire // Mś_13.8 //
children.translated_text: but those for whom emptiness is a view — they were declared incurable. || <s>Mś</s> 13.8 ||
14. Examination of Contact (<s>Saṃsarga</s>) — the fourteenth chapter.

children.text: draṣṭavyaṃ darśanaṃ draṣṭā trīṇyetāni dviśo dviśaḥ /
children.translated_text: The seen, the seeing, and the seer — these three, two by two
and all [together] — do not enter into contact with one another. || <s>Mś</s> 14.1 ||

children.text: evaṃ rāgaśca raktaśca rañjanīyaṃ ca dṛśyatām /
children.translated_text: Likewise, let desire, the desirous one, and the desirable be examined;

children.text: traidhena śeṣāḥ kleśāśca śeṣāṇyāyatanāni ca // Mś_14.2 //
children.translated_text: the remaining <s>kleśas</s> and the remaining <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) [should be examined] in the same threefold manner. || <s>Mś</s> 14.2 ||
Contact of one with another — but that otherness does not exist
for the seen and the rest — therefore they do not enter into contact. || <s>Mś</s> 14.3 ||
And it is not merely that otherness of the seen [and the rest] does not exist;
the otherness of anything whatsoever with anything else is not established. || <s>Mś</s> 14.4 ||
The other is other in dependence on the other; without the other, the other is not other;
and that which depends on something — it is not coherent [to call it] other than that. || <s>Mś</s> 14.5 ||
If the other were other apart from the other, it would exist apart from the other;
the other is not other apart from the other — and therefore it does not exist. || <s>Mś</s> 14.6 ||
Otherness does not exist in the other, nor does it exist in the non-other;

children.text: avidyamāne cānyatve nāstyanyadvā tadeva vā // Mś_14.7 //
children.translated_text: and when otherness does not exist, there is neither 'other' nor 'the same.' || <s>Mś</s> 14.7 ||

children.text: na tena tasya saṃsargo nānyenānyasya yujyate /
children.translated_text: Contact of that with that, or of one with another, is not coherent;

children.text: saṃsṛjyamānaṃ saṃsṛṣṭaṃ saṃsraṣṭā ca na vidyate // Mś_14.8 //
children.translated_text: that which is being contacted, the contacted, and the contactor — [none of these] exist. || <s>Mś</s> 14.8 ||
15. Examination of Intrinsic Nature (<s>Svabhāva</s>) — the fifteenth chapter.
The arising of intrinsic nature from causes and conditions is not coherent;
an intrinsic nature arisen from causes and conditions would be fabricated. || <s>Mś</s> 15.1 ||

children.text: svabhāvaḥ kṛtako nāma bhaviṣyati punaḥ katham /
children.translated_text: How indeed could intrinsic nature be called 'fabricated'?

children.text: akṛtrimaḥ svabhāvo hi nirapekṣaḥ paratra ca // Mś_15.2 //
children.translated_text: For intrinsic nature is unfabricated and independent of anything else. || <s>Mś</s> 15.2 ||
In the absence of intrinsic nature, how would there be other-nature?

children.text: svabhāvaḥ parabhāvasya parabhāvo hi kathyate // Mś_15.3 //
children.translated_text: For the intrinsic nature of another is called 'other-nature.' || <s>Mś</s> 15.3 ||
Apart from intrinsic nature and other-nature, whence then is an entity?

children.text: svabhāve parabhāve vā sati bhāvo hi sidhyati // Mś_15.4 //
children.translated_text: For an entity is established only when intrinsic nature or other-nature exists. || <s>Mś</s> 15.4 ||
If the entity is not established, non-entity too is not established;
for people call the becoming-otherwise of an entity 'non-entity.' || <s>Mś</s> 15.5 ||

children.text: svabhāvaṃ parabhāvaṃ ca bhāvaṃ cābhāvameva ca /
children.translated_text: Those who see intrinsic nature, other-nature,

children.text: ye paśyanti na paśyanti te tattvaṃ buddhaśāsane // Mś_15.6 //
children.translated_text: entity, and non-entity — they do not see the truth in the <s>Buddha's</s> teaching. || <s>Mś</s> 15.6 ||
In the Instruction to <s>Kātyāyana</s>, both 'it exists'
and 'it does not exist' were rejected by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, who discerns being and non-being. || <s>Mś</s> 15.7 ||
If something existed by its own nature, its non-existence would never occur;
for the becoming-otherwise of [something's] own nature is never established. || <s>Mś</s> 15.8 ||
If there is no own nature, of what will there be becoming-otherwise?

children.text: prakṛtau kasya ca satyāmanyathātvaṃ bhaviṣyati // Mś_15.9 //
children.translated_text: If there is own nature, of what will there be becoming-otherwise? || <s>Mś</s> 15.9 ||
'It exists' is the grasping of eternalism; 'it does not exist' is the view of annihilationism;
therefore the wise one should not depend on [either] existence or non-existence. || <s>Mś</s> 15.10 ||

children.text: asti yaddhi svabhāvena na tannāstīti śāśvatam /
children.translated_text: That which exists by intrinsic nature and does not not-exist — that is eternalism;
'It does not exist now but existed before' — annihilationism follows from this. || <s>Mś</s> 15.11 ||
16. Examination of Bondage and Liberation (<s>Bandhamokṣa</s>) — the sixteenth chapter.

children.text: saṃskārāḥ saṃsaranti cenna nityāḥ saṃsaranti te /
children.translated_text: If <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned things) transmigrate — they do not transmigrate as permanent [entities];

children.text: saṃsaranti ca nānityāḥ sattve 'pyeṣa samaḥ kramaḥ // Mś_16.1 //
children.translated_text: nor do impermanent [entities] transmigrate — the same sequence [of argument applies] to a being too. || <s>Mś</s> 16.1 ||
If a <s>pudgala</s> (person) transmigrates — sought in the five [ways among] the aggregates, sense-bases, and elements,

children.text: pañcadhā mṛgyamāṇo 'sau nāsti kaḥ saṃsariṣyati // Mś_16.2 //
children.translated_text: it does not exist — who then will transmigrate? || <s>Mś</s> 16.2 ||
If one transmigrates from appropriation to appropriation, it would be destruction;

children.text: vibhavaścānupādānaḥ kaḥ sa kiṃ saṃsariṣyati // Mś_16.3 //
children.translated_text: and [if] destroyed and without appropriation — what is that, and what will transmigrate? || <s>Mś</s> 16.3 ||
The <s>nirvāṇa</s> of <s>saṃskāras</s> is in no way established;
the <s>nirvāṇa</s> of a being is also in no way established. || <s>Mś</s> 16.4 ||
Neither bound nor liberated are [entities] that are subject to arising and ceasing;

children.text: saṃskārāḥ pūrvavatsattvo badhyate na na mucyate // Mś_16.5 //
children.translated_text: <s>saṃskāras</s> — as before — and a being: [they are] not bound and not liberated. || <s>Mś</s> 16.5 ||
If bondage is appropriation — one with appropriation is not bound;
one without appropriation is not bound [either] — in what state then is one bound? || <s>Mś</s> 16.6 ||
Let bondage bind if you wish — if it exists prior to what is bound;

children.text: na cāsti tat śeṣamuktaṃ gamyamānagatāgataiḥ // Mś_16.7 //
children.translated_text: but it does not [exist] — the rest has been stated [in the analysis of] what is being gone to, what has been gone to, and what has not yet been gone to. || <s>Mś</s> 16.7 ||

children.text: baddho na mucyate tāvadabaddho naiva mucyate /
children.translated_text: What is bound is not liberated; what is not bound is certainly not liberated;
if what is bound were being liberated, bondage and liberation would be simultaneous. || <s>Mś</s> 16.8 ||
'I shall pass into <s>nirvāṇa</s> without appropriation; <s>nirvāṇa</s> will be mine' —
those who hold this — theirs is a great grasping at appropriation. || <s>Mś</s> 16.9 ||
Where there is neither the superimposition of <s>nirvāṇa</s> nor the removal of <s>saṃsāra</s> —

children.text: yatra kastatra saṃsāro nirvāṇaṃ kiṃ vikalpyate // Mś_16.10 //
children.translated_text: what <s>saṃsāra</s> is there, and what <s>nirvāṇa</s> is conceptualized? || <s>Mś</s> 16.10 ||
17. Examination of <s>Karma</s> and Fruit (<s>Karmaphala</s>) — the seventeenth chapter.
The mind that restrains the self and benefits others —

children.text: maitraṃ sa dharmastadbījaṃ phalasya pretya ceha ca // Mś_17.1 //
children.translated_text: that is friendliness; that is <s>dharma</s>; that is the seed of the fruit, both hereafter and here. || <s>Mś</s> 17.1 ||
'Volition (<s>cetanā</s>) and what is willed' — thus was <s>karma</s> spoken of by the supreme sage;
the manifold division of that <s>karma</s> has been proclaimed. || <s>Mś</s> 17.2 ||
Therein, what is called 'volition' — that <s>karma</s> is remembered as mental;

children.text: cetayitvā ca yattūktaṃ tattu kāyikavācikam // Mś_17.3 //
children.translated_text: and what is called 'having willed' — that is bodily and verbal. || <s>Mś</s> 17.3 ||
Verbal expression, non-restraints, and those called '<s>avijñaptis</s>' (non-informative [actions]) —
there are also other <s>avijñaptis</s>, remembered as restraints likewise. || <s>Mś</s> 17.4 ||
Merit resulting from enjoyment, and demerit of the same kind,

children.text: cetanā ceti saptaite dharmāḥ karmāñjanāḥ smṛtāḥ // Mś_17.5 //
children.translated_text: and volition — these seven <s>dharmas</s> are remembered as the essences of <s>karma</s>. || <s>Mś</s> 17.5 ||
If <s>karma</s> persists until the time of ripening, it would have the nature of permanence;

children.text: niruddhaṃ cennirūddhaṃ satkiṃ phalaṃ janayiṣyati // Mś_17.6 //
children.translated_text: if it has ceased — having ceased, what fruit will it produce? || <s>Mś</s> 17.6 ||
The continuum that proceeds from the seed, beginning with the sprout —

children.text: tataḥ phalamṛte bījātsa ca nābhipravartate // Mś_17.7 //
children.translated_text: from that, the fruit [arises]; without the seed, that [continuum] does not proceed. || <s>Mś</s> 17.7 ||
Since from the seed there is the continuum, and from the continuum the arising of the fruit —

children.text: bījapūrvaṃ phalaṃ tasmānnocchinnaṃ nāpi śāśvatam // Mś_17.8 //
children.translated_text: the fruit is preceded by the seed; therefore it is neither annihilated nor eternal. || <s>Mś</s> 17.8 ||
The mental continuum that proceeds from the mind —

children.text: tataḥ phalamṛte cittātsa ca nābhipravartate // Mś_17.9 //
children.translated_text: from that, the fruit [arises]; without the mind, that [continuum] does not proceed. || <s>Mś</s> 17.9 ||
Since from the mind there is the continuum, and from the continuum the arising of the fruit —

children.text: karmapūrvaṃ phalaṃ tasmānnocchinnaṃ nāpi śāśvatam // Mś_17.10 //
children.translated_text: the fruit is preceded by <s>karma</s>; therefore it is neither annihilated nor eternal. || <s>Mś</s> 17.10 ||
The ten white paths of action are the means of accomplishing <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: phalaṃ kāmaguṇāḥ pañca dharmasya pretya ceha ca // Mś_17.11 //
children.translated_text: the five strands of desire are the fruit of <s>dharma</s>, both hereafter and here. || <s>Mś</s> 17.11 ||
There would be many and great faults even if this conception [were accepted];
since [those faults exist], this very conception is not established here. || <s>Mś</s> 17.12 ||

children.text: imāṃ punaḥ pravakṣyāmi kalpanāṃ yātra yojyate /
children.translated_text: I shall now state the conception that is applicable here,
which has been described by <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Śrāvakas</s>. || <s>Mś</s> 17.13 ||
'The non-destruction' [of <s>karma</s>] — like a promissory note, and <s>karma</s> like a debt;

children.text: caturvidho dhātutaḥ sa prakṛtyāvyākṛtaśca saḥ // Mś_17.14 //
children.translated_text: it is fourfold by its element (<s>dhātu</s>), and by nature indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>). || <s>Mś</s> 17.14 ||

children.text: prahāṇato na praheyo bhāvanāheya eva vā /
children.translated_text: It is not to be abandoned by abandonment, nor is it abandoned only by cultivation;
therefore, through non-destruction, the fruit of <s>karmas</s> arises. || <s>Mś</s> 17.15 ||
If it were to be abandoned by abandonment, or through the transference of <s>karma</s> —
faults would follow — such as the destruction of <s>karma</s> and the like. || <s>Mś</s> 17.16 ||
Of all <s>karmas</s> — both dissimilar and similar —

children.text: pratisaṃdhau sadhātūnāmeka utpadyate tu saḥ // Mś_17.17 //
children.translated_text: one single [non-destruction], belonging to the same element, arises at the time of rebirth-connection. || <s>Mś</s> 17.17 ||

children.text: karmaṇaḥ karmaṇo dṛṣṭe dharma utpadyate tu saḥ /
children.translated_text: That <s>dharma</s> [of non-destruction] arises from <s>karma</s> after <s>karma</s>, while seen [in this life];

children.text: dviprakārasya sarvasya vipakke 'pi ca tiṣṭhati // Mś_17.18 //
children.translated_text: it also persists in the ripening of all [<s>karma</s>] of both types. || <s>Mś</s> 17.18 ||
It ceases either when the fruit is passed, or at death;

children.text: anāsravaṃ sāsravaṃ ca vibhāgaṃ tatra lakṣayet // Mś_17.19 //
children.translated_text: one should characterize the division therein as untainted and tainted. || <s>Mś</s> 17.19 ||

children.text: śūnyatā ca na cocchedaḥ saṃsāraśca na śāśvatam /
children.translated_text: Emptiness — yet not annihilation; <s>saṃsāra</s> — yet not eternalism;
and the non-destruction of <s>karma</s> — this <s>dharma</s> was taught by the <s>Buddha</s>. || <s>Mś</s> 17.20 ||
Why does <s>karma</s> not arise? Because it is without intrinsic nature;
and since it has not arisen, therefore it does not perish. || <s>Mś</s> 17.21 ||
If <s>karma</s> existed by intrinsic nature, it would undoubtedly be eternal;

children.text: akṛtaṃ ca bhavetkarma kriyate na hi śāśvatam // Mś_17.22 //
children.translated_text: and <s>karma</s> would be unfabricated — for what is eternal is not produced. || <s>Mś</s> 17.22 ||
If <s>karma</s> were unfabricated, there would be the fear of encountering what was not done;
and the fault of non-abiding in the holy life would follow. || <s>Mś</s> 17.23 ||

children.text: vyavahārā virudhyante sarva eva na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: All conventions would be contradicted, without doubt;
and the distinction between the doer of merit and the doer of evil would not be coherent. || <s>Mś</s> 17.24 ||
That which has ripened in fruit would ripen again;
since <s>karma</s> is fixed — [this follows] if it is [taken to be] intrinsic. || <s>Mś</s> 17.25 ||

children.text: karma kleśātmakaṃ cedaṃ te ca kleśā na tattvataḥ /
children.translated_text: If this <s>karma</s> is of the nature of <s>kleśas</s> — yet those <s>kleśas</s> are not [real] in truth;

children.text: na cette tattvataḥ kleśāḥ karma syāttattvataḥ katham // Mś_17.26 //
children.translated_text: and if those <s>kleśas</s> are not [real] in truth — how could <s>karma</s> be [real] in truth? || <s>Mś</s> 17.26 ||
<s>Karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> are stated as the conditions of bodies;

children.text: karma kleśāśca te śūnyā yadi deheṣu kā kathā // Mś_17.27 //
children.translated_text: if <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> are empty — what is there to say about bodies? || <s>Mś</s> 17.27 ||
The being obscured by ignorance and fettered by craving —

children.text: sa bhoktā sa ca na karturanyo na ca sa eva saḥ // Mś_17.28 //
children.translated_text: that one is the experiencer, who is neither other than the doer nor identical with it. || <s>Mś</s> 17.28 ||
Since this <s>karma</s> is neither arisen from conditions

children.text: asti yasmādidaṃ karma tasmātkartāpi nāstyataḥ // Mś_17.29 //
children.translated_text: nor arisen without conditions — therefore the doer also does not exist. || <s>Mś</s> 17.29 ||

children.text: karma cennāsti kartā ca kutaḥ syātkarmajaṃ phalam /
children.translated_text: If <s>karma</s> does not exist, and the doer [does not exist] — whence would there be the fruit born of <s>karma</s>?

children.text: asatyatha phale bhoktā kuta eva bhaviṣyati // Mś_17.30 //
children.translated_text: And if the fruit does not exist — whence indeed will there be an experiencer? || <s>Mś</s> 17.30 ||
Just as the teacher creates a magical creation through the power of <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power);

children.text: nirmito nirmimītānyaṃ sa ca nirmitakaḥ punaḥ // Mś_17.31 //
children.translated_text: and that creation creates yet another creation; || <s>Mś</s> 17.31 ||

children.text: tathā nirmitakākāraḥ kartā karma ca tatkṛtam /
children.translated_text: so the doer is like a magical creation, and the <s>karma</s> done by it —
that is like yet another creation created by a creation. || <s>Mś</s> 17.32 ||

children.text: kleśāḥ karmāṇi dehāśca kartāraśca phalāni ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Kleśas</s>, <s>karmas</s>, bodies, doers, and fruits —
are like the form of a <s>Gandharva</s>-city, resembling a mirage or a dream. || <s>Mś</s> 17.33 ||
18. Examination of the Self (<s>Ātman</s>) — the eighteenth chapter.
If the self were the aggregates, it would be subject to arising and ceasing;
if it were other than the aggregates, it would have the character of a non-aggregate. || <s>Mś</s> 18.1 ||
If there is no self, whence indeed will there be 'mine'?
Free from 'mine' and 'I' — through the pacification of the self and what belongs to the self. || <s>Mś</s> 18.2 ||

children.text: nirmamo nirahaṃkāro yaśca so 'pi na vidyate /
children.translated_text: And one who is free from 'mine' and 'I' — that one too does not exist;

children.text: nirmamaṃ nirahaṃkāraṃ yaḥ paśyati na paśyati // Mś_18.3 //
children.translated_text: one who sees one free from 'mine' and 'I' — does not [truly] see. || <s>Mś</s> 18.3 ||
When 'mine' and 'I' are exhausted — both externally and internally —
appropriation ceases; from its exhaustion, there is the exhaustion of birth. || <s>Mś</s> 18.4 ||
From the exhaustion of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s>, liberation; <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> are from conceptualization;
those are from elaboration (<s>prapañca</s>); and elaboration ceases in emptiness. || <s>Mś</s> 18.5 ||
'Self' has been designated, and 'non-self' has been taught;

children.text: buddhairnātmā na cānātmā kaścidityapi deśitam // Mś_18.6 //
children.translated_text: but the <s>Buddhas</s> have also taught that there is neither self nor non-self. || <s>Mś</s> 18.6 ||
That which is to be expressed ceases when the domain of the mind ceases;
for the nature of <s>dharmas</s>, like <s>nirvāṇa</s>, is unarisen and unceased. || <s>Mś</s> 18.7 ||

children.text: sarvaṃ tathyaṃ na vā tathyaṃ tathyaṃ cātathyameva ca /
children.translated_text: Everything is real, or not real, or both real and not real,
or neither not real nor real — this is the <s>Buddha's</s> gradual teaching. || <s>Mś</s> 18.8 ||
Not dependent on another, peaceful, not elaborated by elaborations,
free from conceptual construction, without diversity — this is the characteristic of reality (<s>tattva</s>). || <s>Mś</s> 18.9 ||

children.text: pratītya yadyadbhavati na hi tāvattadeva tat /
children.translated_text: Whatever arises in dependence [on something] — that is indeed not that [thing];

children.text: na cānyadapi tattasmānnocchinnaṃ nāpi śāśvatam // Mś_18.10 //
children.translated_text: nor is it other than that — therefore it is neither annihilated nor eternal. || <s>Mś</s> 18.10 ||
Not of one meaning, not of diverse meanings, not annihilation, not eternalism —
this is the nectar of the teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Lords of the World. || <s>Mś</s> 18.11 ||
When Fully Awakened Ones do not arise, and when <s>Śrāvakas</s> have been extinguished —
the knowledge of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> proceeds independently. || <s>Mś</s> 18.12 ||
19. Examination of Time (<s>Kāla</s>) — the nineteenth chapter.
If the present and the future [exist] in dependence on the past —
the present and the future would depend on the past. //<s>Mś</s> 19.1//
If the present and the future do not exist therein [in the past],
how could the present and the future exist in dependence upon it? //<s>Mś</s> 19.2//
Moreover, without dependence [on the past], the establishment of those two [present and future] is not possible;
therefore, neither the present nor the future time exists. //<s>Mś</s> 19.3//
By this very [argument], the remaining two [times], by the same method in turn,
and [the concepts of] upper, lower, middle, and so forth, and oneness and the like, should be understood. //<s>Mś</s> 19.4//

children.text: nāsthito gṛhyate kālaḥ sthitaḥ kālo na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Time that is non-stationary cannot be grasped; stationary time does not exist;

children.text: yo gṛhyetāgṛhītaśca kālaḥ prajñapyate katham // Mś_19.5 //
children.translated_text: and how can time that is not grasped be designated? //<s>Mś</s> 19.5//
If time depends on an entity (<s>bhāva</s>), whence is time apart from an entity?

children.text: na ca kaścana bhāvo 'sti kutaḥ kālo bhaviṣyati // Mś_19.6 //
children.translated_text: And since no entity whatsoever exists [inherently], how could time come to be? //<s>Mś</s> 19.6//
Chapter 20: Examination of the Assemblage [of Conditions] (<s>Sāmagrīparīkṣā</s>), the twentieth chapter.

children.text: hetośca pratyayānāṃ ca sāmagryā jāyate yadi /
children.translated_text: If the fruit arises from the assemblage (<s>sāmagrī</s>) of cause and conditions,

children.text: phalamasti ca sāmagryāṃ sāmagryā jāyate katham // Mś_20.1 //
children.translated_text: and the fruit exists within the assemblage — how can it be produced by the assemblage? //<s>Mś</s> 20.1//

children.text: hetośca pratyayānāṃ ca sāmagryā jāyate yadi /
children.translated_text: If the fruit arises from the assemblage of cause and conditions,

children.text: phalaṃ nāsti ca sāmagryāṃ sāmagryā jāyate katham // Mś_20.2 //
children.translated_text: and the fruit does not exist within the assemblage — how can it be produced by the assemblage? //<s>Mś</s> 20.2//
If the fruit exists within the assemblage of cause and conditions,

children.text: gṛhyeta nanu sāmagryāṃ sāmagryāṃ ca na gṛhyate // Mś_20.3 //
children.translated_text: it should be apprehended in the assemblage — yet it is not apprehended therein. //<s>Mś</s> 20.3//

children.text: hetośca pratyayānāṃ ca sāmagryāṃ nāsti cetphalam /
children.translated_text: If the fruit does not exist within the assemblage of cause and conditions,
then causes and conditions would be the same as non-causes and non-conditions. //<s>Mś</s> 20.4//
If the cause ceases after having transmitted [its nature] to the fruit,

children.text: yaddattaṃ yanniruddhaṃ ca hetorātmadvayaṃ bhavet // Mś_20.5 //
children.translated_text: then the cause would have a dual nature — that which is transmitted and that which has ceased. //<s>Mś</s> 20.5//
And if the cause ceases without having transmitted [its nature] to the fruit,

children.text: hetau niruddhe jātaṃ tatphalamāhetukaṃ bhavet // Mś_20.6 //
children.translated_text: then the fruit, arising after the cause has ceased, would be without a cause. //<s>Mś</s> 20.6//
If the fruit were to come into being simultaneously with the assemblage,

children.text: ekakālau prasajyete janako yaśca janyate // Mś_20.7 //
children.translated_text: then the producer and the produced would be simultaneous — which is absurd. //<s>Mś</s> 20.7//
If the fruit were to come into being before the assemblage,
then the fruit, being free from cause and conditions, would be without a cause. //<s>Mś</s> 20.8//

children.text: niruddhe cetphalaṃ hetau hetoḥ saṃkramaṇaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: If the fruit [arises] when the cause has ceased, there would be a transference (<s>saṃkramaṇa</s>) from the cause [to the fruit],
and a re-birth of the previously arisen cause would follow. //<s>Mś</s> 20.9//
How could a cause that has ceased and gone to destruction produce an arisen fruit?

children.text: tiṣṭhannapi kathaṃ hetuḥ phalena janayedvṛtaḥ // Mś_20.10 //
children.translated_text: And how could a cause that is still abiding produce a fruit, being enveloped by it? //<s>Mś</s> 20.10//
Or, if it is not enveloped by the fruit, which fruit would it produce?

children.text: na hyadṛṣṭvā vā dṛṣṭvā vā heturjanayate phalam // Mś_20.11 //
children.translated_text: For the cause does not produce the fruit either without having seen [it] or having seen [it]. //<s>Mś</s> 20.11//
There is never any conjunction of a past fruit

children.text: nājātena na jātena saṃgatirjātu vidyate // Mś_20.12 //
children.translated_text: with a past cause, nor with an unborn [cause], nor with a born [cause]. //<s>Mś</s> 20.12//

children.text: na jātasya hyajātena phalasya saha hetunā /
children.translated_text: There is never any conjunction of a born fruit

children.text: nātītena na jātena saṃgatirjātu vidyate // Mś_20.13 //
children.translated_text: with an unborn cause, nor with a past [cause], nor with a born [cause]. //<s>Mś</s> 20.13//

children.text: nājātasya hi jātena phalasya saha hetunā /
children.translated_text: There is never any conjunction of an unborn fruit

children.text: nājātena na naṣṭena saṃgatirjātu vidyate // Mś_20.14 //
children.translated_text: with a born cause, nor with an unborn [cause], nor with a destroyed [cause]. //<s>Mś</s> 20.14//

children.text: asatyāṃ saṃgatau hetuḥ kathaṃ janayate phalam /
children.translated_text: In the absence of conjunction, how does the cause produce the fruit?

children.text: satyāṃ vā saṃgatau hetuḥ kathaṃ janayate phalam // Mś_20.15 //
children.translated_text: And even if there is conjunction, how does the cause produce the fruit? //<s>Mś</s> 20.15//
If the cause is empty of fruit, how does it produce the fruit?
If the cause is not empty of fruit, how does it produce the fruit? //<s>Mś</s> 20.16//
A non-empty fruit will not arise; a non-empty [fruit] will not cease;
that which is unceased and unarisen — that will be the non-empty [fruit]. //<s>Mś</s> 20.17//
How could what is empty arise? How could what is empty cease?
What is empty, too — being unceased and unarisen — would follow [as absurd]. //<s>Mś</s> 20.18//

children.text: hetoḥ phalasya caikatvaṃ na hi jātūpapadyate /
children.translated_text: The identity of cause and fruit is never tenable;

children.text: hetoḥ phalasya cānyatvaṃ na hi jātūpapadyate // Mś_20.19 //
children.translated_text: the difference of cause and fruit is also never tenable. //<s>Mś</s> 20.19//
If there were identity of fruit and cause, then producer and produced would be one;
if there were difference of fruit and cause, the cause would be equal to a non-cause. //<s>Mś</s> 20.20//
What will the cause produce for a fruit that exists by its own nature (<s>svabhāva</s>)?
What will the cause produce for a fruit that does not exist by its own nature? //<s>Mś</s> 20.21//
And for that which is not being produced, the status of being a cause is not tenable;

children.text: hetutvānupapattau ca phalaṃ kasya bhaviṣyati // Mś_20.22 //
children.translated_text: and when the status of being a cause is untenable, whose fruit will there be? //<s>Mś</s> 20.22//
And this assemblage (<s>sāmagrī</s>) of conditions and causes, which [does not produce] itself by itself —

children.text: yā sāmagrī janayate sā kathaṃ janayetphalam // Mś_20.23 //
children.translated_text: how could it produce a fruit? //<s>Mś</s> 20.23//
The fruit is not produced by an assemblage, nor is the fruit produced without an assemblage;

children.text: asti pratyayasāmagrī kuta eva phalaṃ vinā // Mś_20.24 //
children.translated_text: if there is a collection of conditions, whence indeed [is there] a fruit without it? //<s>Mś</s> 20.24//
Chapter 21: Examination of Arising and Dissolution (<s>Saṃbhavavibhavaparīkṣā</s>), the twenty-first chapter.

children.text: vinā vā saha vā nāsti vibhavaḥ saṃbhavena vai /
children.translated_text: Neither apart from nor together with arising (<s>saṃbhava</s>) does dissolution (<s>vibhava</s>) exist;

children.text: vinā vā saha vā nāsti saṃbhavo vibhavena vai // Mś_21.1 //
children.translated_text: neither apart from nor together with dissolution does arising exist. //<s>Mś</s> 21.1//

children.text: bhaviṣyati kathaṃ nāma vibhavaḥ saṃbhavaṃ vinā /
children.translated_text: How indeed could dissolution exist without arising?

children.text: vinaiva janma maraṇaṃ vibhavo nodbhavaṃ vinā // Mś_21.2 //
children.translated_text: Death without birth — dissolution does not exist without origination. //<s>Mś</s> 21.2//
How could dissolution exist together with arising?

children.text: na janmamaraṇaṃ caivaṃ tulyakālaṃ hi vidyate // Mś_21.3 //
children.translated_text: For birth and death do not occur at the same time. //<s>Mś</s> 21.3//

children.text: bhaviṣyati kathaṃ nāma saṃbhavo vibhavaṃ vinā /
children.translated_text: How indeed could arising exist without dissolution?

children.text: anityatā hi bhāveṣu na kadācinna vidyate // Mś_21.4 //
children.translated_text: For impermanence is never absent from entities. //<s>Mś</s> 21.4//
How could arising exist together with dissolution?

children.text: na janmamaraṇaṃ caiva tulyakālaṃ hi vidyate // Mś_21.5 //
children.translated_text: For birth and death do not occur at the same time. //<s>Mś</s> 21.5//
For those two [arising and dissolution], whose establishment neither together with one another

children.text: na vidyate, tayoḥ siddhiḥ kathaṃ nu khalu vidyate // Mś_21.6 //
children.translated_text: nor apart from one another is found — how indeed can their establishment be found? //<s>Mś</s> 21.6//
There is no arising of what is subject to decay, nor is there arising of what is not subject to decay;

children.text: kṣayasya vibhavo nāsti vibhavo nākṣayasya ca // Mś_21.7 //
children.translated_text: there is no dissolution of what is subject to decay, nor dissolution of what is not subject to decay. //<s>Mś</s> 21.7//

children.text: saṃbhavo vibhavaścaiva vinā bhāvaṃ na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Arising and dissolution do not exist apart from an entity (<s>bhāva</s>);

children.text: saṃbhavaṃ vibhavaṃ caiva vinā bhāvo na vidyate // Mś_21.8 //
children.translated_text: an entity does not exist apart from arising and dissolution. //<s>Mś</s> 21.8//
Arising and dissolution are not tenable for what is empty (<s>śūnya</s>);
arising and dissolution are not tenable for what is non-empty (<s>aśūnya</s>). //<s>Mś</s> 21.9//
It is not tenable that arising and dissolution are one [and the same];
it is not tenable that arising and dissolution are different. //<s>Mś</s> 21.10//
Arising and dissolution may indeed be seen [to occur],

children.text: dṛśyate saṃbhavaścaiva mohādvibhava eva ca // Mś_21.11 //
children.translated_text: but arising and dissolution are seen only through delusion. //<s>Mś</s> 21.11//
An entity does not arise from an entity, nor does an entity arise from a non-entity;
a non-entity does not arise from a non-entity, nor does a non-entity arise from an entity. //<s>Mś</s> 21.12//

children.text: na svato jāyate bhāvaḥ parato naiva jāyate /
children.translated_text: An entity does not arise from itself, nor does it arise from another;

children.text: na svataḥ parataścaiva jāyate, jāyate kutaḥ // Mś_21.13 //
children.translated_text: it does not arise from both itself and another — then whence does it arise? //<s>Mś</s> 21.13//
For one who accepts [the inherent existence of] an entity, the views of eternalism and annihilationism

children.text: prasajyate sa bhāvo hi nityo 'nityo 'tha vā bhavet // Mś_21.14 //
children.translated_text: follow — for that entity would be either permanent or impermanent. //<s>Mś</s> 21.14//
For one who accepts [the existence of] an entity, there is neither annihilation nor permanence;
for existence is the continuum of arising and decay of the fruit and cause [series]. //<s>Mś</s> 21.15//
If existence is the continuum of arising and decay of fruit and cause,
then, since what has decayed does not arise again, the annihilation of the cause would follow. //<s>Mś</s> 21.16//
For what exists by its own nature, non-existence is not tenable;
and at the time of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, annihilation [would result] from the cessation of the continuum of existence. //<s>Mś</s> 21.17//

children.text: carame na niruddhe ca prathamo yujyate bhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: If the last [existence] has ceased, a first existence is not tenable;

children.text: carame nāniruddhe ca prathamo yujyate bhavaḥ // Mś_21.18 //
children.translated_text: if the last [existence] has not ceased, a first existence is [also] not tenable. //<s>Mś</s> 21.18//
If, while the last [existence] is ceasing, the first [existence] arises,
then the one ceasing would be different from the one arising. //<s>Mś</s> 21.19//
And if it is not tenable that something is ceasing and arising [at the same time],

children.text: sārdhaṃ ca mriyate yeṣu teṣu skandheṣu jāyate // Mś_21.20 //
children.translated_text: then one is born in those very aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>) in which one dies. //<s>Mś</s> 21.20//

children.text: evaṃ triṣvapi kāleṣu na yuktā bhavasaṃtatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, in all three times, the continuum of existence is not tenable;

children.text: triṣu kāleṣu yā nāsti sā kathaṃ bhavasaṃtatiḥ // Mś_21.21 //
children.translated_text: that which does not exist in the three times — how can that be a continuum of existence? //<s>Mś</s> 21.21//
Chapter 22: Examination of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>Tathāgataparīkṣā</s>), the twenty-second chapter.

children.text: skandhā na nānyaḥ skandhebhyo nāsmin skandhā na teṣu saḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s> is not the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), nor is he other than the aggregates; the aggregates are not in him, nor is he in them;
the <s>Tathāgata</s> does not possess the aggregates — then which is the <s>Tathāgata</s>? //<s>Mś</s> 22.1//
If the <s>Buddha</s> does not exist by his own nature without depending on the aggregates,

children.text: svabhāvataśca yo nāsti kutaḥ sa parabhāvataḥ // Mś_22.2 //
children.translated_text: how could he who does not exist by his own nature exist through another's nature? //<s>Mś</s> 22.2//
That which depends on another's nature is established as non-self (<s>anātman</s>);

children.text: yaścānātmā sa ca kathaṃ bhaviṣyati tathāgataḥ // Mś_22.3 //
children.translated_text: and how could that which is non-self be the <s>Tathāgata</s>? //<s>Mś</s> 22.3//

children.text: yadi nāsti svabhāvaśca parabhāvaḥ kathaṃ bhavet /
