children.translated_text: If there is no own-nature, how could there be another's nature?
Apart from both own-nature and another's nature, who is the <s>Tathāgata</s>? //<s>Mś</s> 22.4//
If some <s>Tathāgata</s> were to exist without depending on the aggregates,
he would now [have to] appropriate them, and would then exist through appropriation. //<s>Mś</s> 22.5//
But there is no <s>Tathāgata</s> whatsoever without depending on the aggregates;

children.text: yaśca nāstyanupādāya sa upādāsyate katham // Mś_22.6 //
children.translated_text: and he who does not exist without appropriation — how will he appropriate? //<s>Mś</s> 22.6//
There is nothing whatsoever that is unappropriated that becomes appropriation;

children.text: na cāsti nirupādānaḥ kathaṃcana tathāgataḥ // Mś_22.7 //
children.translated_text: and there is no <s>Tathāgata</s> whatsoever who is without appropriation. //<s>Mś</s> 22.7//
He who, when sought in five ways, is found to be neither identical with nor different from [the aggregates] —

children.text: upādānena sa kathaṃ prajñapyeta tathāgataḥ // Mś_22.8 //
children.translated_text: how could that <s>Tathāgata</s> be designated through appropriation? //<s>Mś</s> 22.8//
Moreover, this very appropriation does not exist by its own nature;
and that which does not exist by its own nature — how could it exist through another's nature? //<s>Mś</s> 22.9//
Thus, appropriation is empty in every way, and so is the appropriator;

children.text: prajñapyate ca śūnyena kathaṃ śūnyastathāgataḥ // Mś_22.10 //
children.translated_text: how is the <s>Tathāgata</s>, who is empty, designated by means of something empty? //<s>Mś</s> 22.10//
One should not say 'empty,' nor should one say 'non-empty,'

children.text: ubhayaṃ nobhayaṃ ceti prajñaptyarthaṃ tu kathyate // Mś_22.11 //
children.translated_text: nor both, nor neither — these are spoken for the purpose of designation (<s>prajñapti</s>). //<s>Mś</s> 22.11//
In the peaceful [<s>Tathāgata</s>], whence [could there be] the fourfold [view] of eternal, non-eternal, and so forth?

children.text: antānantādi cāpyatra kuntaḥ śānte catuṣṭayam // Mś_22.12 //
children.translated_text: And whence in the peaceful [could there be] the fourfold [view] of finite, infinite, and so forth? //<s>Mś</s> 22.12//
Whoever grasps the dense [view] 'the <s>Tathāgata</s> exists' —
that one, imagining 'he does not exist,' would also conceptualize about one who has passed beyond (<s>nirvṛta</s>). //<s>Mś</s> 22.13//
Regarding this [<s>Tathāgata</s>] who is empty by his own nature, the thought

children.text: paraṃ nirodhādbhavati buddho na bhavatīti vā // Mś_22.14 //
children.translated_text: 'the <s>Buddha</s> exists after death' or 'does not exist' is simply not tenable. //<s>Mś</s> 22.14//
Those who elaborate conceptual constructions (<s>prapañca</s>) about the <s>Buddha</s>, who has transcended elaboration and is imperishable —

children.text: te prapañcahatāḥ sarve na paśyanti tathāgatam // Mś_22.15 //
children.translated_text: all of them, destroyed by conceptual elaboration, do not see the <s>Tathāgata</s>. //<s>Mś</s> 22.15//
Whatever is the own-nature of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, that is the own-nature of this world;
the <s>Tathāgata</s> is without own-nature; this world is without own-nature. //<s>Mś</s> 22.16//
Chapter 23: Examination of Error (<s>Viparyāsaparīkṣā</s>), the twenty-third chapter.
Desire (<s>rāga</s>), hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), and delusion (<s>moha</s>) are said to arise from mental construction (<s>saṃkalpa</s>);
for they arise in dependence upon the errors regarding the pleasant and the unpleasant. //<s>Mś</s> 23.1//
Those which arise in dependence upon the errors regarding the pleasant and the unpleasant —

children.text: te svabhāvānna vidyante tasmāt kleśā na tattvataḥ // Mś_23.2 //
children.translated_text: they do not exist by their own nature; therefore the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) are not [ultimately] real. //<s>Mś</s> 23.2//
The existence and non-existence of the self are not established in any way;

children.text: taṃ vināstitvanāstitve kleśānāṃ sidhyataḥ katham // Mś_23.3 //
children.translated_text: and without that [self], how could the existence and non-existence of the <s>kleśas</s> be established? //<s>Mś</s> 23.3//

children.text: kasyaciddhi bhavantīme kleśāḥ sa ca na sidhyati /
children.translated_text: For these <s>kleśas</s> belong to someone, and that [someone] is not established;

children.text: kaścidāho vinā kaṃcitsanti kleśā na kasyacit // Mś_23.4 //
children.translated_text: without someone, do the <s>kleśas</s> exist for no one? //<s>Mś</s> 23.4//

children.text: svakāyadṛṣṭivat kleśāḥ kliṣṭe santi na pañcadhā /
children.translated_text: Like the view of the self-body (<s>svakāyadṛṣṭi</s>), the <s>kleśas</s> are not found in five ways in the afflicted one;

children.text: svakāyadṛṣṭivat kliṣṭaṃ kleśeṣvapi na pañcadhā // Mś_23.5 //
children.translated_text: like the view of the self-body, the afflicted one is not found in five ways in the <s>kleśas</s>. //<s>Mś</s> 23.5//
The errors regarding the pleasant and the unpleasant do not exist by their own nature;
depending on which errors regarding the pleasant and the unpleasant [do] the <s>kleśas</s> [arise]? //<s>Mś</s> 23.6//
Form, sound, taste, touch, smell, and mental objects (<s>dharmas</s>) — a sixfold

children.text: vastu rāgasya dveṣasya mohasya ca vikalpyate // Mś_23.7 //
children.translated_text: object is imagined for desire, hatred, and delusion. //<s>Mś</s> 23.7//
Form, sound, taste, touch, smell, and mental objects are merely
like a city of the <s>Gandharvas</s>, resembling a mirage or a dream. //<s>Mś</s> 23.8//

children.text: aśubhaṃ vā śubhaṃ vāpi kutasteṣu bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: How could the unpleasant or the pleasant exist
in those which are like illusory persons and comparable to reflections? //<s>Mś</s> 23.9//
Without depending on the pleasant, we designate the unpleasant;
since the pleasant depends [on the unpleasant], the pleasant itself is not tenable. //<s>Mś</s> 23.10//
Without depending on the unpleasant, we designate the pleasant;
since the unpleasant depends [on the pleasant], the unpleasant itself does not exist. //<s>Mś</s> 23.11//

children.text: avidyamāne ca śubhe kuto rāgo bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: When the pleasant does not exist, whence will desire arise?

children.text: aśubhe 'vidyamāne ca kuto dveṣo bhaviṣyati // Mś_23.12 //
children.translated_text: When the unpleasant does not exist, whence will hatred arise? //<s>Mś</s> 23.12//
If the grasping 'permanent' with regard to the impermanent is an error,

children.text: nānityaṃ vidyate śūnye kuto grāho viparyayaḥ // Mś_23.13 //
children.translated_text: since nothing impermanent exists in what is empty, whence is the grasping that is error? //<s>Mś</s> 23.13//
If the grasping 'permanent' with regard to the impermanent is an error,

children.text: anityamityapi grāhaḥ śūnye kiṃ na viparyayaḥ // Mś_23.14 //
children.translated_text: is not the grasping 'impermanent' also an error in what is empty? //<s>Mś</s> 23.14//

children.text: yena gṛṇhāti yo grāho grahītā yacca gṛhyate /
children.translated_text: That by which one grasps, the grasping, the grasper, and that which is grasped —

children.text: upaśāntāni sarvāṇi tasmādgrāho na vidyate // Mś_23.15 //
children.translated_text: all are at peace; therefore grasping does not exist. //<s>Mś</s> 23.15//

children.text: avidyamāne grāhe ca mithyā vā samyageva vā /
children.translated_text: When grasping does not exist — whether false or true —
whose error will there be? Whose non-error will there be? //<s>Mś</s> 23.16//
Errors do not arise for one who is in error;
errors do not arise for one who is not in error. //<s>Mś</s> 23.17//
Errors do not arise for one who is [in the process of] erring;

children.text: vimṛśasva svayaṃ kasya saṃbhavanti viparyayāḥ // Mś_23.18 //
children.translated_text: Examine for yourself — to whom do <s>viparyayāḥ</s> (perverted views) arise? // <s>Mś</s> 23.18 //
How can <s>viparyayāḥ</s> (perverted views) that are unborn come into being?
When <s>viparyayāḥ</s> (perverted views) have not arisen, whence comes one who has gone into perverted views? // <s>Mś</s> 23.19 //

children.text: na svato jāyate bhāvaḥ parato naiva jāyate /
children.translated_text: A thing does not arise from itself, nor does it arise from another;

children.text: na svataḥ parataśceti viparyayagataḥ kutaḥ // Mś_23.20 //
children.translated_text: Since it arises neither from itself nor from another, whence comes one who has gone into perverted views? // <s>Mś</s> 23.20 //

children.text: ātmā ca śuci nityaṃ ca sukhaṃ ca yadi vidyate /
children.translated_text: If <s>ātman</s> (self), purity, permanence, and happiness exist,

children.text: ātmā ca śuci nityaṃ ca sukhaṃ ca na viparyayaḥ // Mś_23.21 //
children.translated_text: then <s>ātman</s> (self), purity, permanence, and happiness are not <s>viparyaya</s> (perverted views). // <s>Mś</s> 23.21 //

children.text: nātmā ca śuci nityaṃ ca sukhaṃ ca yadi vidyate /
children.translated_text: If <s>ātman</s> (self), purity, permanence, and happiness do not exist,

children.text: anātmāśucyanityaṃ ca naiva duḥkhaṃ ca vidyate // Mś_23.22 //
children.translated_text: then non-self, impurity, impermanence, and suffering also do not exist. // <s>Mś</s> 23.22 //
Thus <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) ceases through the cessation of <s>viparyaya</s> (perverted views);
when <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) has ceased, <s>saṃskārāḥ</s> (volitional formations) and the rest cease. // <s>Mś</s> 23.23 //

children.text: yadi bhūtāḥ svabhāvena kleśāḥ keciddhi kasyacit /
children.translated_text: If <s>kleśāḥ</s> (afflictions) of anyone exist by their own nature,

children.text: kathaṃ nāma prahīyeran kaḥ svabhāvaṃ prahāsyati // Mś_23.24 //
children.translated_text: how could they ever be abandoned? Who can abandon what has an intrinsic nature? // <s>Mś</s> 23.24 //
If <s>kleśāḥ</s> (afflictions) of anyone do not exist by their own nature,

children.text: kathaṃ nāma prahīyeran ko 'sadbhāvaṃ prahāsyati // Mś_23.25 //
children.translated_text: how could they ever be abandoned? Who can abandon what does not have existence? // <s>Mś</s> 23.25 //
24. Examination of the Noble Truths — the twenty-fourth chapter.

children.text: yadi śūnyamidaṃ sarvamudayo nāsti na vyayaḥ /
children.translated_text: If all this is <s>śūnya</s> (empty), there is no arising and no passing away;
then the non-existence of the four <s>āryasatyāni</s> (noble truths) follows for you. // <s>Mś</s> 24.1 //

children.text: parijñā ca prahāṇaṃ ca bhāvanā sākṣikarma ca /
children.translated_text: Full understanding, abandonment, cultivation, and direct realization —
these are not possible given the non-existence of the four <s>āryasatyāni</s> (noble truths). // <s>Mś</s> 24.2 //
In the absence of those, the four <s>āryaphalāni</s> (noble fruits) also do not exist;

children.text: phalābhāve phalasthā no na santi pratipannakāḥ // Mś_24.3 //
children.translated_text: without the fruits, there are no fruit-abiders and no path-attainers. // <s>Mś</s> 24.3 //

children.text: saṃgho nāsti na cetsanti te 'ṣṭau puruṣapudgalāḥ /
children.translated_text: If those eight kinds of persons do not exist, there is no <s>Saṃgha</s> (community);
and due to the non-existence of the <s>āryasatyāni</s> (noble truths), the true <s>Dharma</s> also does not exist. // <s>Mś</s> 24.4 //

children.text: dharme cāsati saṃghe ca kathaṃ buddho bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: If neither <s>Dharma</s> nor <s>Saṃgha</s> exists, how will there be a <s>Buddha</s>?

children.text: evaṃ trīṇyapi ratnāni brūvāṇaḥ pratibādhase // Mś_24.5 //
children.translated_text: Speaking thus, you contradict the three <s>ratnāni</s> (jewels). // <s>Mś</s> 24.5 //
You contradict <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), the real existence of fruits, <s>adharma</s> (non-virtue) and <s>dharma</s> (virtue) as well,
and all the worldly conventions. // <s>Mś</s> 24.6 //

children.text: atra brūmaḥ śūnyatāyāṃ na tvaṃ vetsi prayojanam /
children.translated_text: To this we say: you do not understand the purpose of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness),

children.text: śūnyatāṃ śūnyatārthaṃ ca tata evaṃ vihanyase // Mś_24.7 //
children.translated_text: <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) itself, and the meaning of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) — therefore you are thus frustrated. // <s>Mś</s> 24.7 //
The <s>dharmadeśanā</s> (teaching of the Dharma) by the <s>Buddhāḥ</s> (Buddhas) is based upon two truths:

children.text: lokasaṃvṛtisatyaṃ ca satyaṃ ca paramārthataḥ // Mś_24.8 //
children.translated_text: <s>lokasaṃvṛtisatya</s> (conventional truth of the world) and <s>paramārthasatya</s> (truth in the ultimate sense). // <s>Mś</s> 24.8 //
Those who do not understand the distinction between these two truths

children.text: te tattvaṃ na vijānanti gambhīraṃ buddhaśāsane // Mś_24.9 //
children.translated_text: do not understand the profound reality in the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>. // <s>Mś</s> 24.9 //
Without relying on convention, the ultimate truth cannot be taught;
without arriving at the ultimate truth, <s>nirvāṇa</s> (cessation) is not attained. // <s>Mś</s> 24.10 //
Wrongly understood, <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) destroys the dull-witted,

children.text: sarpo yathā durgṛhīto vidyā vā duṣprasādhitā // Mś_24.11 //
children.translated_text: like a snake wrongly grasped, or a spell wrongly practiced. // <s>Mś</s> 24.11 //
Therefore the mind of the <s>Muni</s> (Sage) turned away from teaching the <s>Dharma</s>,
knowing that this <s>Dharma</s> is difficult for the dull to fathom. // <s>Mś</s> 24.12 //
Whatever fault you attribute to <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness),

children.text: doṣaprasaṅgo nāsmākaṃ sa śūnye nopapadyate // Mś_24.13 //
children.translated_text: that objection does not apply to us — it does not hold for what is <s>śūnya</s> (empty). // <s>Mś</s> 24.13 //

children.text: sarvaṃ ca yujyate tasya śūnyatā yasya yujyate /
children.translated_text: For one for whom <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is coherent, everything is coherent;

children.text: sarvaṃ na yujyate tasya śūnyaṃ yasya na yujyate // Mś_24.14 //
children.translated_text: for one for whom <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is not coherent, nothing is coherent. // <s>Mś</s> 24.14 //
You, projecting your own faults onto us,
are like one who, having mounted a horse, has forgotten the very horse he rides. // <s>Mś</s> 24.15 //
If you perceive the existence of all things in terms of <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature),
then you see all things as without causes and conditions. // <s>Mś</s> 24.16 //

children.text: kāryaṃ ca kāraṇaṃ caiva kartāraṃ karaṇaṃ kriyām /
children.translated_text: You thereby contradict the effect, the cause, the agent, the instrument, the action,

children.text: utpādaṃ ca nirodhaṃ ca phalaṃ ca pratibādhase // Mś_24.17 //
children.translated_text: arising, cessation, and the fruit. // <s>Mś</s> 24.17 //
That which is <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), we declare to be <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness);
that is a dependent designation, and that itself is the <s>madhyamā pratipad</s> (middle path). // <s>Mś</s> 24.18 //
There is no <s>dharma</s> (thing) whatsoever that has arisen without depending [on something];

children.text: yasmāttasmādaśūnyo hi dharmaḥ kaścinna vidyate // Mś_24.19 //
children.translated_text: therefore there is no <s>dharma</s> (thing) whatsoever that is non-empty. // <s>Mś</s> 24.19 //
If all this is non-empty, there is no arising and no passing away;
then the non-existence of the four <s>āryasatyāni</s> (noble truths) follows for you. // <s>Mś</s> 24.20 //
How will <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering) arise without having originated dependently?

children.text: anityamuktaṃ duḥkhaṃ hi tatsvābhāvye na vidyate // Mś_24.21 //
children.translated_text: <s>Duḥkha</s> (suffering) has been declared to be impermanent — it does not exist in what has intrinsic nature. // <s>Mś</s> 24.21 //
How can what exists by its own nature originate again?
Therefore <s>samudaya</s> (origination) does not exist for one who rejects <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). // <s>Mś</s> 24.22 //

children.text: na nirodhaḥ svabhāvena sato duḥkhasya vidyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Nirodha</s> (cessation) of <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering) that exists by its own nature is not possible;
due to clinging to <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature), you contradict cessation. // <s>Mś</s> 24.23 //
If there were intrinsic nature, the cultivation of the <s>mārga</s> (path) would not be possible;

children.text: athāsau bhāvyate mārgaḥ svābhāvyaṃ te na vidyate // Mś_24.24 //
children.translated_text: but if that <s>mārga</s> (path) is to be cultivated, then it does not have intrinsic nature. // <s>Mś</s> 24.24 //

children.text: yadā duḥkhaṃ samudayo nirodhaśca na vidyate /
children.translated_text: When <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering), <s>samudaya</s> (origination), and <s>nirodha</s> (cessation) do not exist,
what <s>mārga</s> (path) will lead to the cessation of suffering? // <s>Mś</s> 24.25 //
If non-understanding [of suffering] exists by its own nature, then how could there be

children.text: parijñānaṃ nanu kila svabhāvaḥ samavasthitaḥ // Mś_24.26 //
children.translated_text: full understanding of it? Does not <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) remain fixed? // <s>Mś</s> 24.26 //
Likewise for you, abandonment, direct realization, and cultivation

children.text: parijñāvanna yujyante catvāryapi phalāni ca // Mś_24.27 //
children.translated_text: are not possible, just as full understanding is not — nor are the four fruits. // <s>Mś</s> 24.27 //
A fruit that has not been attained by its own nature — how then
can it be possible to attain it for one who grasps at <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature)? // <s>Mś</s> 24.28 //

children.text: phalābhāve phalasthā no na santi pratipannakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Without fruits, there are no fruit-abiders and no path-attainers;

children.text: saṃgho nāsti na cetsanti te 'ṣṭau puruṣapudgalāḥ // Mś_24.29 //
children.translated_text: if those eight kinds of persons do not exist, there is no <s>Saṃgha</s> (community). // <s>Mś</s> 24.29 //
Due to the non-existence of the <s>āryasatyāni</s> (noble truths), the true <s>Dharma</s> also does not exist;

children.text: dharme cāsati saṃghe ca kathaṃ buddho bhaviṣyati // Mś_24.30 //
children.translated_text: if neither <s>Dharma</s> nor <s>Saṃgha</s> exists, how will there be a <s>Buddha</s>? // <s>Mś</s> 24.30 //

children.text: apratītyāpi bodhiṃ ca tava buddhaḥ prasajyate /
children.translated_text: It follows for you that the <s>Buddha</s> [arises] even without depending on <s>bodhi</s> (awakening),

children.text: apratītyāpi buddhaṃ ca tava bodhiḥ prasajyate // Mś_24.31 //
children.translated_text: and it follows for you that <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) [arises] even without depending on the <s>Buddha</s>. // <s>Mś</s> 24.31 //
One who is by nature not a <s>Buddha</s>, even striving for <s>bodhi</s> (awakening),
will not attain <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) through the practice of the <s>bodhisattva</s> path. // <s>Mś</s> 24.32 //

children.text: na ca dharmamadharmaṃ vā kaścijjātu kariṣyati /
children.translated_text: No one will ever perform either <s>dharma</s> (virtue) or <s>adharma</s> (non-virtue);

children.text: kimaśūnyasya kartavyaṃ svabhāvaḥ kriyate na hi // Mś_24.33 //
children.translated_text: what is to be done by what is non-empty? For <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) does not act. // <s>Mś</s> 24.33 //

children.text: vinā dharmamadharmaṃ ca phalaṃ hi tava vidyate /
children.translated_text: For you, there would be a fruit without <s>dharma</s> (virtue) and <s>adharma</s> (non-virtue);

children.text: dharmādharmanimittaṃ ca phalaṃ tava na vidyate // Mś_24.34 //
children.translated_text: and for you, there is no fruit caused by <s>dharma</s> (virtue) and <s>adharma</s> (non-virtue). // <s>Mś</s> 24.34 //

children.text: dharmādharmanimittaṃ vā yadi te vidyate phalam /
children.translated_text: Or if for you there is a fruit caused by <s>dharma</s> (virtue) and <s>adharma</s> (non-virtue),
how can the fruit arisen from <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> be non-empty for you? // <s>Mś</s> 24.35 //
You contradict all worldly conventions
when you contradict the <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination). // <s>Mś</s> 24.36 //
Nothing would need to be done, action would be uncommenced,
and the agent would be one who does not act — for one who rejects <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). // <s>Mś</s> 24.37 //
The world would be unborn, undestroyed, and immutable,
devoid of its manifold states — if devoid of <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature). // <s>Mś</s> 24.38 //
The attainment of the unattained, the making an end of suffering,

children.text: sarvakleśaprahāṇaṃ ca yadyaśūnyaṃ na vidyate // Mś_24.39 //
children.translated_text: and the abandonment of all <s>kleśāḥ</s> (afflictions) — if non-empty, these do not exist. // <s>Mś</s> 24.39 //
One who sees <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) sees this:

children.text: duḥkhaṃ samudayaṃ caiva nirodhaṃ mārgameva ca // Mś_24.40 //
children.translated_text: <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering), <s>samudaya</s> (origination), <s>nirodha</s> (cessation), and the <s>mārga</s> (path). // <s>Mś</s> 24.40 //
25. Examination of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — the twenty-fifth chapter.

children.text: yadi śūnyamidaṃ sarvamudayo nāsti na vyayaḥ /
children.translated_text: If all this is <s>śūnya</s> (empty), there is no arising and no passing away;
through abandonment or through cessation — whose <s>nirvāṇa</s> (cessation) is intended? // <s>Mś</s> 25.1 //
If all this is non-empty, there is no arising and no passing away;
through abandonment or through cessation — whose <s>nirvāṇa</s> (cessation) is intended? // <s>Mś</s> 25.2 //
Not abandoned, not attained, not annihilated, not eternal,
not ceased, not arisen — this is called <s>nirvāṇa</s> (cessation). // <s>Mś</s> 25.3 //
First, <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not a <s>bhāva</s> (existent thing), for it would then have the characteristics of aging and death;

children.text: prasajyetāsti bhāvo hi na jarāmaraṇaṃ vinā // Mś_25.4 //
children.translated_text: there is no <s>bhāva</s> (existent thing) that exists without aging and death. // <s>Mś</s> 25.4 //

children.text: bhāvaśca yadi nirvāṇaṃ nirvāṇaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: If <s>nirvāṇa</s> were a <s>bhāva</s> (existent thing), <s>nirvāṇa</s> would be <s>saṃskṛta</s> (conditioned);

children.text: nāsaṃskṛto hi vidyate bhāvaḥ kvacana kaścana // Mś_25.5 //
children.translated_text: for no <s>bhāva</s> (existent thing) whatsoever anywhere is <s>asaṃskṛta</s> (unconditioned). // <s>Mś</s> 25.5 //
If <s>nirvāṇa</s> were a <s>bhāva</s> (existent thing), how could it be without <s>upādāna</s> (clinging)?

children.text: nirvāṇaṃ nānupādāya kaścid bhāvo hi vidyate // Mś_25.6 //
children.translated_text: For no <s>bhāva</s> (existent thing) that is without <s>upādāna</s> (clinging) exists. // <s>Mś</s> 25.6 //

children.text: yadi bhāvo na nirvāṇamabhāvaḥ kiṃ bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: If <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not a <s>bhāva</s> (existent thing), could it then be an <s>abhāva</s> (non-existent thing)?

children.text: nirvāṇaṃ yatra bhāvo na nābhāvastatra vidyate // Mś_25.7 //
children.translated_text: Where there is no <s>bhāva</s> (existent thing), neither is there <s>abhāva</s> (non-existence). // <s>Mś</s> 25.7 //
If <s>nirvāṇa</s> were an <s>abhāva</s> (non-existent thing), how could it be without <s>upādāna</s> (clinging)?

children.text: nirvāṇaṃ na hyabhāvo 'sti yo 'nupādāya vidyate // Mś_25.8 //
children.translated_text: For no <s>abhāva</s> (non-existent thing) that is without <s>upādāna</s> (clinging) exists. // <s>Mś</s> 25.8 //
That which moves back and forth — dependently and through <s>upādāna</s> (clinging) —
that very same, without depending and without <s>upādāna</s> (clinging), is taught as <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // <s>Mś</s> 25.9 //
The Teacher declared the abandonment of both <s>bhava</s> (existence) and <s>vibhava</s> (non-existence);

children.text: tasmānna bhāvo nābhāvo nirvāṇamiti yujyate // Mś_25.10 //
children.translated_text: therefore it is fitting that <s>nirvāṇa</s> is neither <s>bhāva</s> (existent) nor <s>abhāva</s> (non-existent). // <s>Mś</s> 25.10 //
If <s>nirvāṇa</s> were both <s>bhāva</s> (existent) and <s>abhāva</s> (non-existent),

children.text: bhavedabhāvo bhāvaśca mokṣastacca na yujyate // Mś_25.11 //
children.translated_text: then <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) would be both <s>bhāva</s> and <s>abhāva</s> — and that is not tenable. // <s>Mś</s> 25.11 //
If <s>nirvāṇa</s> were both <s>bhāva</s> (existent) and <s>abhāva</s> (non-existent),
<s>nirvāṇa</s> would not be without <s>upādāna</s> (clinging), for both [bhāva and abhāva] are with clinging. // <s>Mś</s> 25.12 //
How could <s>nirvāṇa</s> be both <s>bhāva</s> (existent) and <s>abhāva</s> (non-existent)?

children.text: asaṃskṛtaṃ ca nirvāṇaṃ bhāvābhāvau ca saṃskṛtau // Mś_25.13 //
children.translated_text: For <s>nirvāṇa</s> is <s>asaṃskṛta</s> (unconditioned), while <s>bhāva</s> and <s>abhāva</s> are <s>saṃskṛta</s> (conditioned). // <s>Mś</s> 25.13 //
How could <s>nirvāṇa</s> be both <s>bhāva</s> (existent) and <s>abhāva</s> (non-existent)?
Both cannot exist in one place, just as light and darkness [cannot coexist]
The assertion that <s>nirvāṇa</s> is neither <s>abhāva</s> (non-existent) nor <s>bhāva</s> (existent)

children.text: abhāve caiva bhāve ca sā siddhe sati sidhyati // Mś_25.15 //
children.translated_text: can only be established if [both] <s>abhāva</s> and <s>bhāva</s> are established. // <s>Mś</s> 25.15 //

children.text: naivābhāvo naiva bhāvo nirvāṇaṃ yadi vidyate /
children.translated_text: If <s>nirvāṇa</s> is said to be neither <s>abhāva</s> (non-existent) nor <s>bhāva</s> (existent),

children.text: naivābhāvo naiva bhāva iti kena tadajyate // Mś_25.16 //
children.translated_text: by whom is it asserted as 'neither non-existent nor existent'? // <s>Mś</s> 25.16 //
After cessation, it is not asserted that the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) exists;

children.text: na bhavatyubhayaṃ ceti nobhayaṃ ceti nohyate // Mś_25.17 //
children.translated_text: nor that he does not exist, nor both, nor neither — this is not asserted. // <s>Mś</s> 25.17 //
Even while remaining [in life], it is not asserted that the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) exists;

children.text: na bhavatyubhayaṃ ceti nobhayaṃ ceti nohyate // Mś_25.18 //
children.translated_text: nor that he does not exist, nor both, nor neither — this is not asserted. // <s>Mś</s> 25.18 //
There is not the slightest distinction of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) from <s>nirvāṇa</s>;
there is not the slightest distinction of <s>nirvāṇa</s> from <s>saṃsāra</s>. // <s>Mś</s> 25.19 //

children.text: nirvāṇasya ca yā koṭiḥ koṭiḥ saṃsaraṇasya ca /
children.translated_text: The limit of <s>nirvāṇa</s> is the limit of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence);
not even the subtlest difference between them exists. // <s>Mś</s> 25.20 //
Views about what is beyond cessation — [whether it has] an end, etc. — and [whether it is] eternal, etc.,

children.text: nirvāṇamaparāntaṃ ca pūrvāntaṃ ca samāśritāḥ // Mś_25.21 //
children.translated_text: are dependent upon [notions of] a posterior limit and an anterior limit of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // <s>Mś</s> 25.21 //
When all <s>dharmāḥ</s> (things) are <s>śūnya</s> (empty), what is finite? What is infinite?
What is both finite and infinite? What is neither finite nor infinite? // <s>Mś</s> 25.22 //
What is identical? What is different? What is eternal? What is non-eternal?

children.text: aśāśvataṃ śāśvataṃ ca kiṃ vā nobhayamapyataḥ // Mś_25.23 //
children.translated_text: What is both eternal and non-eternal? And what is neither? // <s>Mś</s> 25.23 //
The pacification of all apprehension, the pacification of <s>prapañca</s> (conceptual proliferation) — that is bliss;
no <s>dharma</s> (teaching) whatsoever was taught by the <s>Buddha</s> to anyone, anywhere. // <s>Mś</s> 25.24 //
26. Examination of the Twelve Links — the twenty-sixth chapter.
Enveloped by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), one constructs <s>saṃskārāḥ</s> (volitional formations) of three kinds
for the sake of rebirth, and by those <s>karmāṇi</s> (actions), one goes to a [rebirth] destination. // <s>Mś</s> 26.1 //
<s>Vijñāna</s> (consciousness), conditioned by <s>saṃskārāḥ</s> (volitional formations), enters into a [rebirth] destination;
once <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) has entered, <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) is infused. // <s>Mś</s> 26.2 //
Once <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) is infused, the <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (six sense bases) come into being;
with the arising of the <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (six sense bases), <s>sparśa</s> (contact) proceeds. // <s>Mś</s> 26.3 //

children.text: cakṣuḥ pratītya rūpaṃ ca samanvāhārameva ca /
children.translated_text: Depending on the eye and form, together with attention,
depending on <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form), thus <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) proceeds. // <s>Mś</s> 26.4 //
The conjunction of the three — form, <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), and the eye —

children.text: sparśaḥ saḥ tasmātsparśācca vedanā saṃpravartate // Mś_26.5 //
children.translated_text: that is <s>sparśa</s> (contact); and from that <s>sparśa</s>, <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) proceeds. // <s>Mś</s> 26.5 //
<s>Tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) is conditioned by <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), for one craves for the object of feeling;
while craving, one grasps at <s>upādāna</s> (clinging) of four kinds. // <s>Mś</s> 26.6 //
When there is <s>upādāna</s> (clinging), <s>bhava</s> (becoming) of the clinger proceeds;

children.text: syāddhi yadyanupādāno mucyeta na bhavedbhavaḥ // Mś_26.7 //
children.translated_text: for if one were without <s>upādāna</s> (clinging), one would be liberated and there would be no <s>bhava</s> (becoming). // <s>Mś</s> 26.7 //

children.text: pañca skandhāḥ sa ca bhavaḥ bhavājjātiḥ pravartate /
children.translated_text: That <s>bhava</s> (becoming) is the five <s>skandhāḥ</s> (aggregates); from <s>bhava</s>, <s>jāti</s> (birth) proceeds;
aging, death, suffering, and the like — grief, together with lamentation,
despair, and distress — all this proceeds from <s>jāti</s> (birth);
thus arises this entire mass of <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering). // <s>Mś</s> 26.9 //
The ignorant one constructs <s>saṃskārāḥ</s> (volitional formations), which are the root of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence);
therefore the ignorant one is the agent, but not the wise one, due to seeing reality. // <s>Mś</s> 26.10 //
When <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) has ceased, <s>saṃskārāḥ</s> (volitional formations) do not arise;
the cessation of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) comes through the cultivation of knowledge itself. // <s>Mś</s> 26.11 //
Through the cessation of each [link], the subsequent one does not proceed;
thus this entire mass of <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering) is rightly ceased. // <s>Mś</s> 26.12 //
27. Examination of Views — the twenty-seventh chapter.
The views that 'I existed in the past' and 'I did not exist [in the past]' —
Those views regarding the eternal and so forth, which are based upon the past — (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.1ab)
'I shall not exist' — and what [other] in the future path?
'I shall exist' and so forth — these are based upon the future. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.2)
'I existed in the past' — this is not tenable.

children.text: yo hi janmasu pūrveṣu sa eva na bhavatyayam // Mś_27.3 //
children.translated_text: For the one who [existed] in previous births is not the same as this one. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.3)
If that very self [were the same], then the appropriation (<s>upādāna</s>) would differ;

children.text: upādānavinirmukta ātmā te katamaḥ punaḥ // Mś_27.4 //
children.translated_text: apart from the appropriation, what then would your self be? (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.4)
If it is established that there is no self apart from appropriation,

children.text: syādupādānamevātmā nāsti cātmeti vaḥ punaḥ // Mś_27.5 //
children.translated_text: then the appropriation itself would be the self — but then your self does not exist. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.5)
And the appropriation itself is not the self, for it arises and ceases.
How indeed could the appropriation become the appropriator? (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.6)
And a self different from the appropriation is simply not tenable;

children.text: gṛhyate hyanupādāno yadyanyo na ca gṛhyate // Mś_27.7 //
children.translated_text: for if it were different, it would be grasped without appropriation — but it is not grasped. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.7)
Thus the self is neither different from the appropriation, nor is it the appropriation itself;

children.text: ātmā nāstyanupādānaḥ nāpi nāstyeṣa niścayaḥ // Mś_27.8 //
children.translated_text: the self does not exist without appropriation, nor is it certain that it does not exist. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.8)
'I did not exist in the past' — this is not tenable.

children.text: yo hi janmasu pūrveṣu tato 'nyo na bhavatyayam // Mś_27.9 //
children.translated_text: For the one who [existed] in previous births is not different from this one. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.9)

children.text: yadi hyayaṃ bhavedanyaḥ pratyākhyāyāpi taṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: For if this one were different, he would exist even after rejecting that [former one];

children.text: tathaiva ca sa saṃtiṣṭhettatra jāyeta vāmṛtaḥ // Mś_27.10 //
children.translated_text: and just so, he would remain, or he would be born there as an immortal. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.10)
There would be annihilation of actions, and the destruction of what was done by one
would be experienced by another — and such consequences would follow. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.11)
Nor is 'having come into being without having existed' [tenable], for faults arise here:

children.text: kṛtako vā bhavedātmā saṃbhūto vāpyahetukaḥ // Mś_27.12 //
children.translated_text: the self would either be fabricated, or it would have arisen without a cause. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.12)
Thus the view regarding the past — 'I did not exist,' 'I existed,'

children.text: ubhayaṃ nobhayaṃ ceti naiṣā samupapadyate // Mś_27.13 //
children.translated_text: 'both,' or 'neither' — none of these is tenable. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.13)
In the future path, what [are] the views 'I shall exist'
and 'I shall not exist'? These are the same as [the views concerning] the past. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.14)

children.text: sa devaḥ sa manuṣyaścedevaṃ bhavati śāśvatam /
children.translated_text: If 'that god is this human,' then eternalism would follow;

children.text: anutpannaśca devaḥ syājjāyate na hi śāśvatam // Mś_27.15 //
children.translated_text: and the god would be unborn, for what is eternal is not born. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.15)
If the human were different from the god, then non-eternalism would follow;
and if the human were different from the god, then [karmic] continuity would not be tenable. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.16)
If one part were divine and one part were human,

children.text: aśāśvataṃ śāśvataṃ ca bhavetacca na yujyate // Mś_27.17 //
children.translated_text: it would be both non-eternal and eternal — and that is not tenable. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.17)
If both the non-eternal and the eternal were established,

children.text: siddhe na śāśvataṃ kāmaṃ naivāśāśvatamityapi // Mś_27.18 //
children.translated_text: then, [with both] established, one could surely [hold that it is] neither eternal nor non-eternal. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.18)
If someone came from somewhere and were to go somewhere else again,

children.text: yadi tasmādanādistu saṃsāraḥ syānna cāsti saḥ // Mś_27.19 //
children.translated_text: then <s>saṃsāra</s> would be beginningless — but that is not the case. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.19)
If nothing is eternal, what would be non-eternal?
And [the view of] both eternal and non-eternal is refuted by both of these. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.20)

children.text: antavān yadi lokaḥ syātparalokaḥ kathaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: If the world were finite, how would the other world come about?
And if the world were infinite, how would the other world come about? (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.21)
Since this continuity of the <s>skandha</s>s (aggregates) proceeds
like the [succession of] flames of a lamp, neither finitude nor infinitude is tenable. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.22)
If the previous [<s>skandha</s>s] were destroyed and these

children.text: skandhāḥ skandhān pratītyemānatha loko 'ntavān bhavet // Mś_27.23 //
children.translated_text: <s>skandha</s>s, depending on those, were not to arise, then the world would be finite. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.23)
If the previous [<s>skandha</s>s] were not destroyed and these
<s>skandha</s>s, depending on those, were not to arise, then the world would be infinite. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.24)
If one part were finite and one part were infinite,
the world would be both finite and infinite — and that is not tenable. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.25)
How could one part of the appropriator be destroyed

children.text: na naṅkṣyate caikadeśa evaṃ caitanna yujyate // Mś_27.26 //
children.translated_text: and one part not be destroyed? This is not tenable. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.26)
And how could one part of the appropriation be destroyed
and one part not be destroyed? This too is not tenable. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.27)
If both the finite and the infinite were established,
then, [with both] established, one could surely [hold] neither finite nor infinite. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.28)
Or rather, since all entities are empty (<s>śūnya</s>), the [views of] eternal and so forth —

children.text: kva kasya katamāḥ kasmātsaṃbhaviṣyanti dṛṣṭayaḥ // Mś_27.29 //
children.translated_text: where, of whom, which ones, and from what would these views arise? (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.29)
I pay homage to <s>Gautama</s> (the Buddha), who, out of compassion,
taught the true <s>Dharma</s> for the abandonment of all views. (<s>Madhyamakakārikā</s> 27.30)
